...wounds, and brought him into the inn. This is a manifest and lively representation of the corruption of man in Paradise, and also of the corruption of the earth under the curse of God when Paradise departed from it.

36. Now, do you wish to be a *Magus* <note>original: "Magus"; a wise man or magician who understands the hidden laws and "signatures" of nature.</note>? Then you must become the *Samaritan* <note>original: "Samaritane"; a reference to the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:25–37).</note>; otherwise, you cannot heal the wounded and decayed. For the body which you must heal is half dead and sorely wounded, and its proper garment is torn off, so that it is very hard for you to recognize the man whom you wish to heal—unless you have the eyes and will of the Samaritan, and seek nothing else but to restore what the wounded man has lost.

37. Now consider! The Eternal Word manifested itself in Adam with divine living essentiality—with the heavenly <term>Mercury</term> <note>In Boehme's system, Mercury represents the active, expressive spirit or "word" within nature.</note>. But when the soul's fire in Adam was poisoned by the infection of the Devil, it corrupted the spirit of the will in Adam. It introduced that will, through the nature of the serpent, into earthly, deadly lust. Then the heavenly Mercury of the heavenly essence withdrew—that is, the soul's will departed from it with its desire and introduced its hunger into the earthly mortal essence, namely, into the property of the cold Mercury which had created stones and earth. Adam’s spirit wanted to test this Mercury and have the knowledge of evil and good, and so this Mercury of the four elements immediately drew him into its poison. It worked effectively in him and robbed him of the divine property; it stung and wounded him with heat and cold, made him half-dead, and stripped him of his angelic raiment. This raiment was the garment in the pure element where the heavenly source penetrates the four elements and tinctured <note>original: "tinctured"; in alchemy, to tincture is to infuse a substance with a new quality or to transform its very nature.</note> them in Adam's body. Then he needed no other garment, for heat and cold were, as it were, swallowed up in him; just as the day holds the night swallowed up in itself, and yet the night dwells in the day, though it is not manifest. This is what happened to man when the property and source of the night seized him; then it dominated him. And thus it also happened with the earth when God cursed it.

38. Now, do you wish to be a *Magus*? Then you must understand how to change the night again into the day; for the source of the night (namely, of the darkness) is the anguish-source of death, and the source of the day (namely, of the light) is the life and the luster within that life. Now Christ has again rekindled this shine in humanity and quickened man again in himself. Now, if you wish to tincture, then you must change that which is shut up and closed in the death of the night back into the day; for the day is the tincture, and yet the day and night lie within each other as one essence.

<margin>† Or, what should I first do to make this happen?</margin>
39. Now Reason asks, "How can I begin † to do this?" Look at the process of how God began with humanity when He wanted to <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "Tincture"; in Boehme's alchemy, to tincture is to infuse a substance with a higher spiritual power to transform and heal it.</note> it.

40. Christ came into this world in our restricted human form and brought the tincture of life—that is, the Deity—into the enclosed fortress of death. He came into the world as a pilgrim in our poor form; He became one of us so that He might transform us within Himself. But what did He do? Did He live in joy? Did He behave and carry Himself like a lord? No. He entered into death and died, and through us, He put away the <term>source of night</term> <note>original: "Nights-Source"; the darkness or state of spiritual death.</note> within Him. But how did He do it? He joined the essence of our soul and body to the divine essence and brought our essence to life with the divine. Because of this, our essence entered again with its will and desire into the divine essence, and the heavenly <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat"; the creative command of God, meaning "let it be done."</note> was moved again within humanity. For humanity inclined itself once more toward liberty—that is, toward the free <term>delight</term> <note>original: "Lubet"; from the German *Lust*, referring to God's free will or joyful inclination.</note> of the Deity.

41. After this was done, the man Christ was tempted for forty days, just as the first Adam was alone and tempted in Paradise. During that time, outward earthly food was taken from Him, and His humanity had to eat God's essence through its own desire. Everything that the first Adam had focused his mind on <note>original: "Amused himself in."</note>, everything he had imagined and been captivated by—specifically the death of the "night"—was presented to Christ. The Devil, being the prince of this world, now presented these things to Him in the quality of death, just as he had presented them to Adam through the serpent, which Adam and his wife focused on and entered into with their imagination.

42. Now look! What did Christ do when He was to undergo the struggle of this trial, when the human essence was to enter again with its desire into the Deity and eat of "God's Bread"—that is, of divine substance? He went to the Jordan River and was baptized by John. With what? With the water of the Jordan and with the "water" in the Word of Life—the divine essence. This essence had to transform our mortal essence within the outward humanity of Christ. From this, a divine hunger arose in the human essence, so that He desired to eat of God's bread. Therefore, the Spirit of God took Him and carried Him into the wilderness. There, the Father's <term>property of wrath</term> <note>original: "Fathers Property in the Wrath"; referring to the strict, judging quality of God's nature.</note> opposed Him through the "Prince of Wrath" (the Devil). Both God's bread and the "bread of God's anger" (according to the desire of death) were offered to Him. Now it was tested whether the soul—which was generated and created out of the Father's property—would, after this transformation <note>original: "Tincturation."</note> of baptism, enter again into the desire of love—that is, into the <term>Nothing</term> <note>In Boehme's thought, the "Nothing" or *Ungrund* is the divine abyss of pure freedom and love that exists before and beyond all created things.</note> which is beyond all sources of pain.

43. What is suggested here to the *Magus* <note>original: "Magus"; a spiritual seeker or practitioner of divine alchemy.</note>? A mystery is hinted to him: if he wishes to perform wonders with Christ and transform <note>original: "Tincture"</note> the corrupt body into the new birth, he must first be baptized. Then he develops a hunger for God's bread, and this hunger contains the *Verbum Fiat* <note>original: "Verbum Fiat"; Latin for "the Word: let it be done," referring to God's creative command.</note>—namely, the † *Archeus* <note>original: "Archeus"; in alchemy, the vital force or "master-builder" that directs the growth and healing of a body.</note> of the new generation, which is the *Mercury*. However, I am not speaking here of a priest's baptism; the artist must understand this in a spiritual sense. God and humanity must first come together before you baptize, just as happened in Christ; the Deity first entered into humanity, but humanity could not immediately understand it until it was brought to life through baptism, and the hunger—namely, the "dead Mercury" within the human essence—was stirred up again in the heavenly part.

44. And here human "eating" began again; that is, the *Mercury* once more received divine qualities and will. Then the inner *Mercury* (meaning the human's own nature) tasted the divine word of God's essence. The four elemental qualities fed on the "nature of the night" <note>the state of spiritual darkness or physical limitation</note> until the human *Mercury* refined its life and transformed the four elements into one. Then Life transformed death, which was accomplished on the cross. At that point, the four elements left him; that is, He died to time—namely to the "night," or the four elements—and arose in the pure element, living for eternity.

45. The *Magus* must also follow and observe this process in his alchemy. Do you ask how? I will not spell it out for you because of the wicked, who are not worthy of it. Only observe the baptism: that you baptize the "dead Mercury"—which lies powerless and enclosed within the heavenly essence—with its own baptism. [Notice] what † essence he consists of in a thing. But you must have his divine water as well as the earthly water; for the earthly *Mercury* cannot otherwise receive the *Divine Being* unless the *Divine Mercury* receives some of its power, causing it to stir and hunger. At that point, the heavenly *Mercury* searches but does not yet find divine essence around it for food. Therefore, it brings its will through the desire for death into itself—namely into the *Verbum Fiat* [the creative word] which made and produced it—and focuses its hunger upon it. Thereupon, the * divine essence leans toward it and becomes joy within him. Then begins the start of the new body out of the divine essence, which the desire nourishes and raises. When the new life—the "day"—is born, the four elements die. Then the new body is enclosed in dark death, and on the third day, it rises again.

47. You say, "Tell me of the Baptism?" and I have already told it to you. Every hunger is a desire after its own property. Now, if you give the property of death back to the hunger of death, then death increases. But if you give it heavenly property, then death does not receive it, for hell is set against heaven. Therefore, you must give death and the anger of God to death; and within this anger, give him heavenly essence—namely, the baptism. In this way, the baptism will draw <note>original: "Aval"</note> death into itself. Even then, the anger dies in death through the baptism, but not immediately. You must first follow the "process of Christ" and allow the baptized person to preach—that is, appear in his divine form and colors. Persecute and plague him exceedingly, and give him no rest; for in this way the true *Mercury* <note>original: "Mercury"; the active, vital spirit or transformative principle in both alchemy and the soul.</note> becomes working and active. And when he has shown all his wonders through the old *Adam* <note>original: "Adam"; the fallen, physical human nature that must be overcome.</note>, then you must cast both the old and new man into God’s great anger. Slay the old man, ventilate him, and hang him † naked on the cross. Then take him from there and lay him into the putrefaction—namely, into the grave.

48. And then Christ will arise from death and appear, but only his own people will know him. He walks about in a heavenly form, and sometimes in the same [form which he had here on earth] until the Feast of Pentecost. For now, the highest perfection is tested in him: whether he will persist in the angelic form and eat only of the divine essence. Then comes the Holy Spirit, proceeding with his power out of the whole body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>—that is, out of both the body and soul. This power then transforms <note>original: "Tinctureth"</note> the dead and broken being. This could be seen on the day of Pentecost, where Saint Peter transformed <note>original: "Tinctured"</note> three thousand souls at once with his heavenly *Mercury* and delivered them out of death.

49. Dear seekers, herein lies the Pearl. Had you the Universal <note>original: "Universal"; the "Universal Medicine" or Philosopher's Stone, believed by alchemists to be a cure for all physical and spiritual corruption.</note>, then you could also transform as Saint Peter did; but your greedy death withholds you and shuts you up. For you seek only greed and temporal honor in the pleasures of the flesh, to reproduce yourselves in the nature of the night. Therefore, the Pearl hides itself from you. Yet the day shall appear again when the wrathful anger of God is fulfilled, satisfied, and appeased in the blood of the saints, and turned into a life of love—and that time is near.

<meta>This page continues Boehme’s exploration of the spiritual "process" of transformation, comparing the internal alchemical work to the biological processes of marriage, conception, and pregnancy. # CHAPTER 7. The Signature of All Things <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"</note>.

### The Process.

50. Every creature remains within its own kind during generation and reproduction—the male with the female, and the female with the male. Now, God said to Adam and Eve after the Fall, *“The seed of the woman shall crush the serpent’s head.”* He did not say [the seed] of the man. In this lies the Baptism of Nature: the male possesses the fire-spirit, and the female possesses the water-spirit for the tincture <note>original: "Tincture"; a spiritual or alchemical essence that transforms or colors matter and spirit.</note>. Now, Mercury <note>original: "Mercury"; the active, transformative principle in both alchemy and the soul’s growth.</note> is a fire-life, and he makes a body for himself according to his hunger and desire. The most important part of the work in the beginning is to give this fire-hunger a "Love-Virgin" of its own kind as a companion, so that his wrathful hunger may be changed into love. Then they sleep together in their own marriage bed. Now, the Devil is an enemy of this marriage; he soon arrives with a strange desire and tempts these married people. However, he does not dare to use physical violence against them; he only afflicts and plagues them with a false, strange desire. If they surrender their desire to his will, and his desire overcomes them, they become enemies to one another and produce a false child. For Christ said, *“An evil tree brings forth evil fruit, and a good tree brings forth good fruit.”*

<margin>*Or, She shall, etc.</margin>

51. Therefore, the practitioner <note>original: "Artist"; the alchemist or spiritual seeker performing the work.</note> must be careful and keep himself from such anger, yet he must also prepare a cross for this married couple—for he acts as both their foe and their friend. In this way, they may both lift up their desire to God while in their marriage bed of love. Thus, through their desire, God’s essence may become pregnant within them. Then, in their union, they shall conceive such a child, which they (meaning the mother, namely <note>original: "viz."</note> the female) shall nourish in their belly until it is ripe.

52. In the meantime, let the mother take care that she holds no love for anyone other than her consort, and also that she does not fantasize <note>original: "Imagine"; referring to the historical belief that a mother's mental state could physically alter a developing fetus.</note> about strange things; otherwise, she will leave a spot or mark upon the child. She must remain simply in one love until the child’s body is perfect, which happens in the fourth month. Yet, depending on how the parents share the same properties, strife and conflict will arise within the child's essence when the child is about to receive its soul’s life.

53. But when the essence is in its wrestling combat, the practitioner must assist the soul-like property—namely <note>original: "viz."</note> the fiery property—until the soul-spirit attains its life. At that moment, it appears in a woman’s form and luster. Now the practitioner might assume that he has the child and that it is born, but it requires more time until the soul grows strong; only then does it appear and show itself in its red and white coat <note>These colors refer to the alchemical stages of *albedo* (whiteness/purity) and *rubedo* (redness/perfection).</note>.

54. But there is still a wonderful process yet to come; when the

When the soul's life is born, the new soul casts away the vegetative <note>original: "Vegetable"</note> life of the parents. This vegetative life is propagated and inherited by the body from the parents' biological power <note>original: "Vegitta"</note>, in which the child's body was curdled <note>original: "congealed"</note> and grew until the soul entered. Then the life of the four elements dies, and the life in the "one element" <note>the spiritual quintessence or pure element of paradise</note> arises. The child is hidden in dark death, and the practitioner <note>original: "Artist"; refers here to the alchemist or the soul-seeker</note> assumes it is dead, but he must have patience until the child is born.

->The Specific Process for the Shaping of the Magical Child.<-

55. The journey of Christ on Earth is a true symbol <note>original: "real Type"</note> of how the new child is nourished in the mother’s womb after its conception (as mentioned before), how it attains a vegetative life, and how it grows until the time of its true soul and spirit-life. It shows how the child arises from the essence of its parents, and how—upon the igniting <note>original: "Enkindling"</note> of its own true life—it casts away the parents' biological power <note>original: "Vegitta"</note> and influence. A new plant—a new, specific operation—now arises according to the nature of the newly ignited spirit. Because of this, the child is more noble than its parents; understand this in terms of its outward life.

56. But perhaps some crude, foolish scholar <note>original: "clownish Sophister"</note> might encounter this book and derive a strange misunderstanding from it because I write of a "soul" in the vegetative life. Let him know that we do not mean that the Image of God, which was formed into a likeness of God, exists within metals, stones, and herbs. Rather, we mean the "Magical Soul": how Eternity (the Deity) imprints and portrays itself in its own likeness within all things, according to the model of its wisdom, and how God fills all in all. We mean the Highest Good <note>original: "Summum Bonum"</note>, the good treasure that lies hidden within the essence of the outward world like a Paradise.

57. As Christ in his childhood grew up in both human and divine nature <note>original: "Property"</note> until he was twelve years old, he went with his mother Mary to the feast at Jerusalem. He entered the Temple among the scholars <note>original: "Scribes"</note>, questioned them, listened to them, and gave answers to the teachers' questions. But when his parents returned home, assuming he was among the traveling company, he stayed behind on purpose among the doctors of law. He did not follow the intent of his parents, but rather the divine will, until they came back and searched for him. Then his mother said to him, "My son, why <note>original: "wherefore"</note> have you dealt with us this way? Look, your father and I have been seeking you in sorrow." Then he said to them, "How is it that you searched for me? Did you not know <note>original: "Wist ye not"</note> that I must be about my Father’s business?" And then he went home with them and was subject to them.

58. In this figure, we have the symbol <note>original: "Type"</note> of the wills of the inward and outward world—how they exist within one another and against one another, and yet are but one. This is just as two kingdoms were made manifest in Christ. One worked according to God’s will and broke the outward world's will of his parents when Christ stayed behind in the temple against their wishes. His parents were troubled by this, and the divine will in Christ knew it well enough. The other kingdom—namely, the will of his parents—broke the divine will in the sense that he went home with them and was obedient to them according to their will.

59. This figure shows the practitioner <note>original: "Magus"; a spiritual seeker or alchemist who works with the hidden forces of nature</note> that he will find two wills in the goal he intends to carry out. One will—the divine will—will not be obedient or subject to him. Yet, if his own specific external will rightly applies itself to that goal and seeks only the dear child Jesus with Mary—with desire and earnest sorrow, rather than the earthly pleasure of the flesh—then the divine will will be obedient to him, go home with him, and be used according to his good pleasure.

60. Secondly, it shows him the twofold working and will in all things. If he wishes to be a practitioner <note>original: "Magus"</note> and, according to his own will, turn the essence of the "good property" <note>the inherent spiritual goodness or divine spark in a substance</note> from the inward world into the outward, then he must first be capable of the inward—namely, the divine—will. Otherwise, he cannot change the inward will into the outward. Just as Christ was not obedient to the external will of his mother until she sought him with grief and sorrow of heart, turning her will into God's will, she wrestled with God’s will in his compassion. She was like Jacob, who wrestled the whole night until the Lord blessed him, and God said to him, "You have wrestled with God and man, and have overcome," or gained the victory.

61. Also, let the practitioner <note>original: "Magus"</note> know that he does not need to try to implant the right will for perfection into his purpose from the outside. It is already in all things. He only needs to introduce a divine, desiring will (aligned with the thing's specific property) into the task he takes in hand. This will then wrestles with the divine will, as Jacob did, and blesses the will introduced to God's will. Thus, the divine will yields itself freely into the "hunger" <note>the spiritual longing or attraction</note>, or inclines itself to the desire, and makes the imperfect will (which earnestly presses into his compassion) perfect. Then it is rightly said: "You have wrestled with God and have overcome." Then your purpose obtains a transformed body, which is both heavenly and earthly.

62. Observe this! It is the first beginning of baptism. In this way, you are fit and prepared for baptism, and not otherwise; otherwise...

You baptize only with the water of the outward world; but the true practitioner <note>original: "Magus"</note> baptizes with the outward and inward water. If he has a right divine desire within him, then God's will in his baptism is the first glimmering tinder in *Mercury* <note>In Böhme’s system, Mercury represents the energetic, moving principle of life and nature</note>, so that life kindles death—namely, the *Mercury* that was shut up in death—and he gains a divine desire. Even then, *Mercury* begins to hunger after the divine essence and performs his first miracle, turning the water into wine, just as Christ did after his baptism. This is the first tincturation <note>the process of spiritual infusion or transformation</note> in the dead body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> through the power of baptism, where the vegetative <note>original: "Vegitta"; the active, growing life-force</note> or working energetic life obtains another property—namely, a hunger for love. With this love, she embraces her bridegroom—the "fire-source"—so that he is kindled in her love and changes his cold, deadly wrath and will into a fiery love-will. Then the mortal water turns into wine (a sharpness of both fire and water tastes), from which at last comes an oil for another baptism, according to the manner and disposition of the practitioner—that is, according to what he intends and begins. After the practitioner has joined the virgin and the young man together, then Christ—the bridegroom—is led with his bride into the desert and tempted by the devil.

63. Here is the trial by which the practitioner <note>original: "Artist"</note> is proved by God to see what he seeks with his baptism. For here is the proof in Paradise to test whether the bridegroom is not too corrupt; for the Virgin casts her love upon him and invites him. If he receives it with desire and gives his will to it, then she gives him her heart and will entirely. This is the heavenly tincture, which gives itself into the kindled anger of God (namely, into the curse of the earth when God cursed it); that is, into the *Mercury* enclosed in death, which is the bridegroom. For the "seed of the woman"—the heavenly tincture—must bruise the head of the serpent—the poisonous *Mercury* in the state of death—and change his poison into wine; only then does the Virgin receive the seed of the bridegroom.

64. The desert is the earthly, outward body where *Mercury* is tempted. When the devil appears to *Mercury* and plagues him, assaulting him in his fiery essence, then the Virgin must come to help him and give him her love. Now, if *Mercury* eats of the virgin-like love—that is, of God’s bread—then he may stand before the devil; and at last, the angels come to him and serve him. The enlightened practitioner <note>original: "Magus"</note> will well understand what is meant by the "devil."

Whatever he begins, he must follow through with. Only the bridegroom is wonderful: He continually has two wills, that is <note>original: "viz."</note>, an earthly hunger after God's anger and a hunger after his bride. Therefore, he must always be given his own earthly food—not into his belly, but magically—so that he may satisfy only his will's hunger. His food is his mother who conceives him, as mentioned before.

68. In short, the entire Work which people talk so much about consists of two things: a heavenly and an earthly. The heavenly must transform the earthly within it into something heavenly; Eternity must transform Time within itself into Eternity. The practitioner seeks <term>Paradise</term>; if he finds it, he has the greatest treasure on earth. But one dead man does not raise another; the practitioner must be living if he wants to say to the mountain, "Rise, and throw yourself into the sea."

Then it is dark and unvalued, and it is despised and mocked that such a mystery should lie hidden in such a humble form. There, Christ walks in a poor, simple form upon the earth as a pilgrim, and he does not even have enough property in Saturn to lay his head. He walks as a stranger, as if he were not at home there.

71. ...situated in *Mercury*, namely a pleasant habitation, and gives him its goodwill. In the <term>Flagrat</term> <note>original: "Flagrat"; a term Boehme uses for a sudden, explosive burst of spiritual or physical light/fire that causes a transformation.</note> of *Mars*, the highest life ignites itself and separates into two essences: out of the Love comes a body, and out of the Fire comes a spirit. Then the life of Love sinks downward within the fiery Flagrat and appears beautiful, but it is *Venus*, a woman. 

At this point, the Artist <note>The practitioner of alchemy or spiritual transformation.</note> believes he has found the treasure, but the hungry *Mercury* devours *Venus*, and the child turns into a <term>black Raven</term> <note>The "black raven" represents *nigredo*, the alchemical stage of decomposition or "death" necessary for rebirth.</note>. <margin>*</margin> Then *Mars* afflicts *Mercury* within himself until he grows faint and surrenders himself to death. For in the property of *Mars*, the light is ignited, and the true life is born. It stands within the pure element, where neither anger nor death can destroy it.

72. It seems strange to human reason that God followed such a process in the restoration of humanity through Christ—that He appeared in such a poor, undervalued form in our human nature, and was reviled, mocked, scorned, scourged, crucified, and killed; and that He was buried and rose again from the grave, walking forty days upon the earth before He entered into His invisible kingdom. Reason is so blind that it understands nothing of the Eternal Birth; it knows nothing of Paradise, how Adam was once there, how he fell, or what the "curse of the earth" truly is. If reason understood this, the whole process would be obvious. As the Eternal Birth is in itself, so is the process of restoration after the Fall; likewise, the process the wise men use with their <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>A legendary substance in alchemy capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life; for Boehme, it is a symbol of Christ and spiritual perfection.</note> is exactly the same. There is not the slightest difference between them, for all things originally arise out of the Eternal Birth, and all must be restored in one and the same manner.

73. Therefore, if the <term>Magus</term> <note>A seeker or practitioner of spiritual mysteries.</note> wishes to seek and find Paradise within the curse of the earth, he must first walk in the person of Christ. God must be manifest in him—specifically in the internal man—so that he may have "magical sight." He must treat his goal as the world treated Christ; then he may find Paradise, where there is no death.

<margin>*</margin> 74. But if he is not part of this birth of restoration, and does not walk the path Christ walked upon the earth—if he does not step into the will and spirit of Christ—then let him give up and stop his seeking. He will find nothing but death.

### CHAPTER VIII.

->*Of the fiery Sulfurous Seething <note>original: "Seething"; the boiling or bubbling activity of life-force within the earth.</note> of the Earth, and how*<-
->*growth occurs in the Earth; also of the Separation*<-
->*of the several Kinds of Creatures: An open*<-
->*Gate for the Wise Seekers.*<-

1. Let the reader only consider what was written before concerning the Center of the Generation <note>The source or origin from which all things are produced.</note> of all Essences, and then he may easily proceed here: everything that is corporeal—whether it be Spirit or Body—consists of a sulfurous property <note>In alchemy, "Sulphur" represents the active, fiery, and expansive principle of life.</note>. The Spirit exists in such a spiritual property, and the Body, created out of the Spirit, exists in such a corporeal property.

<margin>* Mute, senseless, without feeling.</margin>
2. For all things have arisen from the Eternal Spirit as a likeness of the Eternal. The invisible Essence, which is God and Eternity, has, through its own Desire, introduced itself into a visible Essence and manifested itself within Time. Thus, He is like a Life within Time, and Time is within Him as if it were *dead*. Just as a Master makes his work with an instrument, and the instrument—being senseless <note>original: "senseless"; lacking its own consciousness or will.</note>—is mute to the Master, yet it is the means of the making and the Master alone guides it; even so are all things confined within limit, measure, and weight according to the Eternal Generation. They run on in their operation and generation according to the right and property of Eternity.

3. And God has appointed over this great Work only one

The Master and Protector, who alone can manage the Work, is His *officer*—namely, the Soul of the Great World <note>original: "Soul of the great World"; also known as the *Anima Mundi*, a spiritual essence that many Renaissance thinkers believed resided within and animated the physical earth.</note>—in which all things exist. God has appointed a likeness of Himself as the Reason to rule over this Officer; this is the Understanding, God’s own dominion, with which He rules the Officer. Now, the Understanding shows the Officer the property of each thing, and how the separation and degrees proceed from each other. For all things are † contained within the Sulphurous Body <note>In Boehme's alchemy, "Sulphur" represents the inner substance or "oil" of a thing that holds its energy.</note>, and *Mercury* <note>In this context, "Mercury" is the active, moving spirit or life-force.</note> is the life of the *Sulphur*. The Salt is the "Impression" <note>Boehme uses "Salt" to describe the force of solidification or physical manifestation that gives spirit a form.</note> that preserves the \* **Body** from falling into ashes, so that the Spirit is revealed in a physical essence.

4. The property of *Mercury* exists in *Sulphur* like the boiling of water; *Sulphur* is the water in which *Mercury* seethes, and it continually produces two forms out of that water. One is oily and living, coming from the freedom of the divine power's property; the other is mortal, coming from the dissolution in the fire during the "salnitral flash" <note>original: "Salnitral Flagrat"; Boehme’s term for a sudden, explosive burst of spiritual energy, similar to lightning or the ignition of saltpeter, which marks the transition from darkness to light or death to life.</note>.

5. The oily property is found in stones, metals, herbs, trees, beasts, and humans. The mortal property is in the earth, the water, the fire, and the air. Likewise, the oily property exists within these four forms (earth, water, fire, and air) as a spirit or life; these four properties are like a dead body in which the Oil is a light or life. From this, the Desire—that is, Growth—arises, springing out of the dead property. This is the Vegetative Life: a springing, budding, and growing out of death.

6. However, the oily property could not be a "Life" if it were not in the anguish <note>original: "Anguish"; for Boehme, this is a technical term (*Angst*) representing the productive tension and friction required for life to manifest and move forward.</note> of death. This anguish makes it sprout or move, because its will is to flee from and press out of that anguish. It forces itself eagerly forward, and from this, growth arises. Thus, death must be a cause of life, so that life may be active; therefore, *Mercury* is the true moving life.

7. In the mortal property, he is evil and is called the life of death, of hell, and the anger of God. In the oily property, he is good, due to the power of the gentleness and freedom of God. He is the Officer’s craftsman <note>original: "*Faber*"; Latin for "smith" or "craftsman," representing the creative force that shapes matter.</note>, by which the Officer distinguishes the degrees in the Vegetative Life, separating the living being from the mortal, and the heavenly essence from the dead or earthly. He orders it into two kingdoms: the Good in the oily property into a heavenly being (that is, into a Light), and the mortal part into the darkness.

8. These two kingdoms are in a continual combat with one another, and there is an incessant wrestling within them, like water...

8. ...boiling on the fire; each boils in its own property. Namely, the oily property boils in joy and meekness, and the mortal property <note>In Boehme’s alchemy, "oily" represents the life-giving spiritual light, while "mortal" or "anxious" represents the harsh, dark material force.</note> boils in the anguish of darkness. For meekness is like a stillness, but the source of anguish elevates <note>original: "sublimeth"; an alchemical term for purifying or raising a substance from a solid to a spiritual state</note> it and turns it into pleasant laughter. <margin>* with, or in.</margin>
9. And yet we do not acknowledge that the oily property takes any poisonous source into itself. Rather, *Mercury* (the fire-life) <note>In this context, *Mercury* represents the active, driving spirit or will of a living thing.</note> insinuates itself into the anguish and poisons the Essence of Time, which the outward *Mercury* creates through its own desire. That is, it departs from the inward oily essence; then the internal being remains immovable in itself, and the essence and spirit of Time sever from the essence and spirit of Eternity. And yet there is no actual dividing; both principles remain in one essence, even though they are two distinct essences. One does not comprehend the other, just as eternity does not comprehend time. This is also how Adam and Eve died: the soul's *Mercury* departed with its imagination <note>Boehme uses "imagination" to mean the formative power of the soul's desire or will.</note> from the essence of eternity into the essence of time (the source of anguish). Then the essence of eternity lost its leader. Christ restored this again * by the divine Word, or *Mercury*, so that the essence of eternity—which in Adam was forsaken by the soul's *Mercury*—obtained life again.

10. Thus we know that the essence of eternity lies hidden in the anxious *Mercury*, as if in the fortress of death. Our writing and teaching is to show how a person may bring the poisonous *Mercury* and its desire to enter once again into the essence of eternity (the "Enclosed" <note>The "Enclosed" refers to the hidden spiritual reality currently shut off from fallen humanity.</note>) and resume the essence of eternity as a body. Through the same tincture <note>In alchemy, a "tincture" is a spiritualizing or transforming power that changes the quality of a substance.</note>, one can bring the essence of time and reconcile them as one, so that the whole body <note>original: *Corpus*</note> of the inward and outward world may be only one. Thus, there may be only one will in the spirit—a hunger for love. This hunger then creates for itself only one essence, and every spirit eats of its own essence or body, so that afterward no evil will can ever arise there again.

11. Thus we understand that joy and sorrow, love and enmity, originally arise through imagination and longing; for...

If his poisonous will can be † introduced into that same spirit of love, then he reveals the pearl himself, for he transforms himself. 13. For there is a continual † struggle within the earth. Eternity strives with longing through time to be free from vanity. In its longing, it gives itself to *Mercury* as its life and master craftsman <note>original: *Faber*; Latin for "smith" or "craftsman"</note>. When *Mercury* obtains this in his hunger, he becomes joyful and makes this free inclination <note>original: *Lubet*; a term for the divine "pleasure" or "will" that desires to manifest</note> physical within himself. From this arise gold and silver, along with other metals and good herbs, all according to the powerful effectiveness of each place. Just as the * *boiling* <note>original: *Sude*; the alchemical "seething" or natural process of formation</note> occurs in each place, so too is the metal formed, following the property of the seven forms of nature. They must also very exactly understand and know the property of the patient—specifically, which of the seven forms of nature represents the *Mercury* within the *Sulphur*, for that determines the "salt" <note>In alchemy, Salt represents the physical body or the solid manifestation of the interaction between Mercury and Sulphur.</note> he produces. Now, if the physician gives the patient a contrary salt, *Mercury* is only more vehemently enraged and made more poisonous. 

But if he receives his own salt according to his own property (which he hungers for), then * he rejoices and readily leaves behind his poisonous source in the fire of *Mars* <note>Mars represents the harsh, wrathful, or "fiery" aspect of nature.</note>. The true physician, however, has another method of cure: he first brings the *Mercury* he intends to use out of the "anguish of death" and into "liberty." He may truly † cure, whereas the other way is dangerous and uncertain. If the other happens to cure, it is by chance and is very inconsistent; he cannot cure any disease fundamentally. This is because the outward *Mercury* is limited; it cannot reach further than the four elements into the mortal essence. It is able to do nothing in the *sidereal* body <note>original: *Sydereal*; the astral or spiritual body that is distinct from the physical flesh.</note>.

The Sun’s power leans with great desire toward the highest heavenly tincture <note>A "tincture" is a spiritual essence or transforming force that changes the quality of a substance.</note> and draws it in—pulling it out of the earthly body and into a solar one. Thus, the Sun draws the power out of the root in the earth, and the joyful *Mercury* ascends along with it. *Mercury* continually draws the Sun’s power down from above into itself, and from beneath, it draws its mother—the *sulphur* <note>original: Brimstone</note>—to itself. Here, all the seven forms of nature <note>The "seven forms" are Boehme's fundamental qualities of existence: desire, motion, anguish, light, sound, etc.</note> arise in joyfulness during the struggle, as each wants to be dominant. This is how taste is formed in the generation of nature. Whichever form of nature becomes the chief determines the taste of the Salt in the *sulphur*, and that determines what kind of herb grows out of the earth. Although everything springs from its "mother" [the earth/sulphur], this is how all things took their origin, and how they still do today.

This is its "Signature," showing what kind of form is internally in the essence, in the source. The white color of the **branch** <note>original: *Branch*</note> is from the freedom of the *love-delight* <note>original: *Love-Lubet*; Boehme's term for the joyful inclination or "will" of divine love</note>, and the brown is the earthly property from **Saturn’s** impression and from the wrath of **Mars**. The green, which opens itself above, belongs to **Mercury** in the form of **Jupiter** and **Venus**.

<margin>† Or, In their wrestling combat.</margin>
19. For **Jupiter** is power, and **Venus** is love-desire, which hasten toward the **Sun** as toward their own likeness. The **Heaven**, which is created out of the midst of the **Water**, puts upon them its blue and green-colored garment according to the power of the **Stars**; for the **Spirit** of the **Stars** also receives the new child, gives him its own **Spirit** and **Body**, and rejoices in him. Now the forms are in † contest, and **Mercury** is the *craftsman* <note>original: *Faber*; Latin for craftsman or creator</note> and separator. **Saturn** impresses (compresses) the form, and **Jupiter** is the pleasant power in the **Sulphur**. **Mars** is the fire-source—that is, the might in the **Sulphur**. **Venus** is the **Water**—that is, the sweet desire. **Mercury** is the life, **Luna** <note>the Moon</note> is the body, and **Sol** <note>the Sun</note> is the heart—the center toward which all forms tend and press.

20. Thus the outward **Sun** presses into the **Sun** within the herb, and the inward **Sun** presses into the outward one, and there is a pure, pleasing relish and delight of one essence in another. **Saturn** makes it sour; **Jupiter** makes a pleasant taste; **Mars** makes it bitter because of his anxious nature; **Venus** makes it sweet; **Mercury** distinguishes the taste; and **Luna** takes it into her "sack" <note>likely referring to the physical container or matrix of the plant</note> and nurtures it. For **Luna** has both an earthly and heavenly property, and she provides the *medium* <note>original: *Menstruum*; in alchemy, a solvent or base liquid that carries a "tincture"</note> in which the *spiritual essence* <note>original: *Tincture*</note> lies.

21. Thus there is a stimulation in the taste; each form hastens toward the sweet water and the **Sun**. **Jupiter** is pleasant and ascends upward with the love-desire in the sweet source-water. In this water, **Mars** rages and thinks himself to be master of the house, seeing that he rules the fire-spirit in the **Sulphur**. **Mercury** is dismayed that **Mars** disquiets him so much, and **Saturn** makes the *flash* <note>original: *Flagrat*; a sudden discharge or "crack" of energy during the meeting of opposing forces</note> corporeal according to his austere impression. These [conflicts] are the knots upon the stalk. The *flash* is *salnitral* <note>original: *Salnitral*; referring to the energetic property of saltpeter</note>, according to the third form of **Nature** in the first impression of the spirit-life—that is, in the form of anguish from which the **Sulphur** takes its origin. In that *flash*, **Mercury** goes up in the *saltpeter* energy on the sides and takes **Venus** (the love-desire) into it, from which grow twigs and branches.

Brethren, this is how you must cure: not with the angry **Mercury**, which in many herbs is a source of evil poison, but with the inward **Mercury**. Understand that this is done by that part of the heavenly property; for gold cannot be made out of the earth alone, or out of the deadened property in the saltpeter <note>original: *Salniter*</note>, because there is no "fixedness" <note>Alchemical stability or permanence</note> within it.

For it is the same in the earth: where **Mercury** is alive in his mother (that is, in the **Sulphur**) and is not held back so that he may reach **Venus** in his hunger for food, the Sun will soon shine forth; for it beams forth in the meekness of **Venus**. He cooks <note>original: "dresseth or seeths"</note> his food with his own fire and needs no Artist for that—which the Artist must well observe—for he has his **Mars** within himself.

# CHAPTER 8. The Signature of All Things <note>original: *Signatura Rerum*</note>

Essence [or Being] is all God’s, be it evil or good; for from Him and through Him are all things. What is not of His Love is of His Anger. Paradise is still in the world, but man is not in it unless he be born again of God; then, as to that new regeneration, he is within it, and not with the Adam of the four elements <note>The "Adam of the four elements" refers to the physical, mortal body made of earth, air, fire, and water, as opposed to the spiritual body.</note>. Oh, that we would but once learn to know ourselves, and even understand it by looking at created essence [or being].

43. Look! In Saturn <note>In alchemy, Saturn refers to the metal lead. Böhme uses the alchemical belief that lead contains the "seed" of gold to explain how divine light is hidden within base matter.</note> there lies gold shut up in a very lowly and contemptible form and manner, which indeed resembles no metal; and even if it is cast into the fire and melted, yet a man shall have nothing except a contemptible matter devoid of any form of virtue, until the artist takes it in hand and uses the right process upon it; only then is it revealed what was inside it.

<margin>Or, so it is signed or marked.</margin>
44. Likewise, God dwells in all things, but the thing knows nothing of God. He is similarly not manifest to the thing, and yet it receives power from Him. The Good is also in it, but it is as if it were wholly shut up [or hidden] by iniquity [or evil]. You have an example of this in bushes and other thorny and pricking briars, out of which a beautiful, well-smelling blossom nevertheless grows. Two properties lie within them: namely, a pleasant one and an unpleasant one. Whichever one overcomes the other is what shapes [forms or marks] the fruit.

Thus, the hunger of the false Serpent began to work effectively in him, and Death awoke in him, and then Paradise hid itself within him. For Paradise entered into itself, and the poison of the Serpent in Death’s property also dwelt in itself. ## CHAPTER IX.

### Of the *Signature* <note>original: "Signatura Rerum," meaning the "Signature of All Things."</note>, showing how the *Internal* characterizes the *External*.

1. The entire outward visible world, with all its existence, is a <term>signature</term> <note>A physical mark or form that reveals the inner spiritual essence of a thing.</note> or figure of the inward spiritual world. Whatever is internal, and however its operation works, it likewise has its character externally. Just as the spirit of each creature displays and manifests the internal form of its birth <margin>* In, or with.</margin> by its body, so does the Eternal Being as well.

2. The Being of all beings is a wrestling power; for the kingdom of God consists in power, as does the outward world. Therefore, God has appointed six days for man to work, and the seventh day is the perfection in which the six find rest. It is the center toward which the desire of the six days tends. This is why God calls it the Sabbath or day of rest, for within it the six forms of the working power rest. It is the divine *sound* <note>original: "Sound," interpreted as voice or harmony.</note> in the power, or the kingdom of joy, in which all the other forms are made manifest. Just as the desire of the inward forms has made itself external, the internal being is present in the external. The internal holds the external before it like a mirror <note>original: "Glass"</note>, in which it beholds itself in the quality of the generation of all forms; the external is its signature.

4. Thus, everything that is generated out of the internal has its signature. This can be seen in all living creatures—in the shape and form of the body, in their behavior and deportment, and also in their sound, voice, and speech. It is the same in trees and herbs, in stones and metals; everything is formed according to how the wrestling occurs in the power of the spirit. The figure of the body is represented this way, and its will remains this way as long as it is active and "boiling" in the life-spirit.

This is to be recognized by the signature; therefore, the physician who understands the signature is best suited to gather the herbs himself.

48. An herb with the aforementioned property does not grow tall; it is somewhat rough to the touch. 49. Every living creature, according to its kind in the aforementioned property, is friendly and pleasant if you deal with it friendly and gently. In this way, both of these angry adversaries may submit their will to *Jupiter’s* will, so that *Jupiter*, *Mars*, and *Mercury* may all three obtain one single will in their power. Then the cure is correct, and the Sun of Life will again kindle itself in this union and agreement; it will also balance the nausea of the disease in the conflict within the Salt of the disease, and turn *Mercury's* poison and *Mars's* bitter fire into a pleasant *Jupiter*.

58. For example: an honest man falls into great debts, care, trouble, and distress, which afflicts him almost to death. This is also true in the mental soul <note>original: "mental Soul"; Böhme uses this to describe the soul as a thinking, spiritual essence influenced by the "planets" or properties of nature</note>.

He must transform <term>tincture</term> the soul’s *Mercury* again with love, and then his *Sun* will again shine in the soul, and his *Jupiter* will rejoice.

61. Now if you say that you cannot do this, and that you are too strongly captivated, I also say that I cannot. For it lies not in my willing, running, and toiling, but it lies in the compassion of God. For I cannot by my own strength and ability overcome the wrathful anger of God which is ignited in me. But seeing that his dear Heart <note>referring to Christ</note> has freely given itself again out of love—and in love—into humanity (that is, into the poisonous, ignited *Mercury* in the soul), and has transformed <term>tinctured</term> the soul (that is, the poison-source of the eternal nature in the eternal Father’s nature), therefore I will cast my will into his transformative power <note>original: "Tincture"</note>. I will go with my will out of the ignited poison-source, out of the evil *Mercury* in God's anger, and into his death. With my corrupted will, I will die with him in his death and become a "nothing" in him, and then he must be my life.

<margin>* Or, At the goal.</margin>
62. For if my will is a "nothing," then he is in me whatever he pleases, and then I no longer know myself, but only him. And if he wills that I shall be "something," then let him effect it. But if he does not will it, then I am dead in him, and he lives in me as he pleases. And so, if I am a nothing, then I am at the end <note>at the goal or state of rest</note>.

### CHAPTER 9. THE SIGNATURE OF ALL THINGS <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"</note>

...in the essence out of which my father **Adam** was created; for out of nothing, God has created all things.

63. This "Nothing" <note>Böhme’s concept of the "Nothing" (often called the *Ungrund*) refers to the absolute, undifferentiated state of the Divine before it manifests in creation—a state of pure potential and peace.</note> is the highest good, for there is no *Turba* <note>original: "Turba"; a term Böhme uses for the "turmoil" or "disturbance" that leads to destruction and wrath in nature</note> within it, and so nothing can touch or bother my soul. I am a "nothing" to myself, but I belong to God, who knows what I am; I do not know it, nor should I need to know it.

64. And this is the cure for my soul's sickness. Anyone who will take this risk with me will find by experience what God will make of them. For example: I am writing this here, and yet I am also not the one doing it. For as myself, I know nothing and have not learned or studied these things; therefore, I am not the one doing it, but God does it in me as he pleases.

65. I am unknown to myself, but I am known to him according to his will. Thus, I do not live for myself, but for him. In this way, we are only one in Christ, like a tree with many boughs and branches; he begets and brings forth the fruit in every branch as he pleases. Thus, I have brought his life into mine, so that I am at one <note>original: "Atoned"; here meaning "at-one," or reconciled in unity</note> with him in his love. His will in Christ has entered into the humanity within me, and now my will enters into his humanity. In this way, his living *Mercury*—that is, his Word, specifically the speaking *Mercury* <note>the creative power of God’s voice</note>—colors <note>original: "Tinctureth"; in alchemy, to "tincture" is to transform the inner essence or quality of a substance</note> my own wrathful, evil *Mercury* and transforms it into his own. Thus my *Mars* <note>the planetary property of fire, energy, or anger</note> has become a love-fire of God, and his *Mercury* speaks through mine, as if through his instrument, whatever he pleases. My *Jupiter* <note>the planetary property of wisdom, reason, and joy</note> lives in divine joy, though I do not realize it; the true Sun shines for me, though I do not see it. I do not live for myself, see for myself, or know for myself. I am a thing, and I know not what; for God knows what I am. So now I move and act like a vessel in which the Spirit drives or acts through me as he pleases; thus, I live according to my inward will, which is not actually mine.

<margin>† Or, I am an enemy.</margin>
66. Yet I still find another life within me, which I am—not according to this *resignation* <note>original: "Resignation [or Self-denyal]"; the spiritual practice of surrendering the individual will to the Divine</note>, but according to the creaturely nature of this world—that is, according to the likeness of eternity. ## CHAPTER X.

### *Of the Inward and Outward Cure of Man.*

<margin>1.</margin> Let the lover of God understand us correctly; we do not rely on a historical, heathenish conjecture, but only and alone upon the light of outward nature; both suns <note>Böhme refers to the "outward sun" of the physical world and the "inward sun" of divine revelation/spiritual insight.</note> shine for us. Understand us correctly and see! How God cured man when the poison of the serpent and the devil held him imprisoned in death, and how he still cures the poor soul held captive in God’s anger; the physician must use a similar process in curing the outward body.

2. The divine light and love were extinguished in Adam because he focused his imagination <note>original: "Imagined into"; meaning to direct one's will or desire toward something</note> into the serpent’s property—namely, into evil and good—so that the poison of death began to work effectively in Mercury <note>In Böhme’s alchemical language, Mercury represents the active, moving spirit or the "Word" expressed in nature.</note>, and the source of anger was inflamed in the eternal Mars <note>Mars represents the fiery, forceful, and potentially wrathful aspect of nature.</note>, and the dark impression of eternal nature’s property took possession of him. His body became earth in the dark impression within the poison of the ignited Mercury, and was at enmity with God. He was utterly undone, and there was no remedy for him by any creature, neither in heaven nor in this world; wrathful death captivated him in soul and body.

3. Now, how did God cure him and transform <note>original: "Tincture"; an alchemical term for imbuing something with a new spiritual quality or "color"</note> him again? Understand this: in man was the *Expressed Word*, which I call the eternal Mercury in man; for it is the true, ruling, and acting life. It was inspired or spoken into man’s image (which God created out of his essence into an image according to God) as into a created image. This was the soul, with the properties of all the three worlds: namely, the world of light and understanding, which is God; the fire-world, which is the eternal nature of the Father of all beings; and the light, love-world, which is heavenly corporality—for the essence, namely the corporality, exists within the desire of love.

4. The desire of love is spirit and is the heart of God—namely, the true divine understanding. Now when Mercury <note>In Böhme’s system, Mercury represents the active, moving spirit in both nature and the soul.</note> awakens from the "death" caused by the restriction of Saturn <note>Saturn represents the cold, hardening, and materializing principle.</note> and receives Manna into the mouth of its own nature from that poisonous source of death, then the *Flagrat* <note>original: *Flagrat*; a term Böhme uses for a sudden ignition, flash, or "shattering" moment of transformation from darkness to light.</note> of the Kingdom of Joy arises. It is like a light kindled in the darkness, for Joy or Love springs up in the midst of Wrath. Now, if Mercury catches a glimpse of the Love within Mars <note>Mars represents the fiery, energetic, and often wrathful principle.</note>, then that Love overwhelms the wrath. This is a type of transmutation, though it is not yet fixed or permanent; as soon as this happens, the properties of the angels begin to come into view and understanding.

### The Process in the Temptation.

22. Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, and the Devil came to him and tempted him. When the soul of Christ was hungry, the Devil said to Jesus, "Open the center within the stones—that is, the restricted Mercury—and make bread for yourself; eat the substance of the soul’s own nature. What? Will you eat nothing? Will you not eat of the Speaking Word? Eat instead of the Manifested Word <note>original: "expressed Word"; the physical world of matter and duality.</note>—that is, the properties of Good and Evil—and then you will be lord over both." This was the same "bite" that Adam took, in which he ate death. Then Jesus Christ said:
> "Man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God."

23. Take note! From where did the person of Christ receive the will to refuse to eat (with the soul’s hunger) the bread that could have been made from stones—a feat he certainly could have performed? What would have happened if the hunger of his human nature—after the anointing of his baptism—had eaten during the temptation of the Mercury within the "impression of death"? That is, what if he had eaten the Sulphur <note>original: *Sulphur*; here meaning the vital substance or "oil" of the physical world.</note> of the Manifested Word, which contained the Wrath and from which Love had fled, as is the case in all earthly things?

24. Observe! The will and desire to eat of the "Speaking Word" entered the soul’s nature through the movement of the Deity. When the Deity moved itself within the essence of the soul—which had been "shut up in death" within his mother Mary’s essence or seed—it introduced the vision of God’s Eye (the Love) into the essence of the dead soul and manifested Love within Death. Then, one Divine property desired the other. The desire of the physical hunger to eat of God’s bread or essence arose from his Baptism. When the "water of the body"—which was enclosed in death within the hardening of substance—tasted the Water of Eternal Life in the Holy Spirit (that is, the Holy Spirit’s physical or essential reality during the Baptism), then the spark of divine hunger and the burning desire for God’s essence arose in his flesh. This was a divine hunger: a glimmering or shining spark of the Divine nature.

25. Now, the man Christ had to be tempted in both body and soul regarding what he would choose to eat. On the other side, the Speaking Word <note>The pure, creative source of divine power.</note> in its quality of Love was presented to his soul and body.

26. Here began the combat that *Adam* should have faced in Paradise. On one side, God’s desire for Love, which had revealed itself in the soul, eagerly reached for the qualities of the soul and body. It introduced its desire into the soul’s nature so that the soul might eat of it and give the body Manna. On the other side, the Devil—acting within God’s quality of wrath—assaulted the soul’s nature. He brought his imagination into the property of the "First Principle" <note>In Böhme’s system, the First Principle is the dark, fiery foundation or "root" of existence.</note>—that is, into the center of the dark world, which is the soul’s fire-life.

27. The contest was over the Image of God: whether it would live in God’s Love or Anger, in the Fire or the Light. He said to the Devil, "*It is written: You shall not tempt the Lord your God.*" <note>Matthew 4:7</note> This is the same as if he had said: A creature of God must neither will nor do anything except what God wills and does through it. There must be no other God to rule and will besides the only One. The creature must move and act as the Will-Spirit of God leads it; it must be God’s instrument, through which He works and does only what He pleases.

34. It creates not Manna, but Earth; as we may see in the wild Earth, which was produced in the "enkindling" or movement of the Father in his fire-property. In this inflammation (that is, in the poisonous wrath of the *manifested Mercury*), the Devil thought he would be a prince. Indeed, he is the prince of that specific property in the wicked, and also in the government of the world when it acts in wrath. But God holds him captive with the Water and Light of the third Principle <note>Böhme’s term for the material world, which is governed by both divine light and the "dark" fire of nature.</note>, so that he is not the prince of the entire manifested Word, but merely the judge's executioner. He must watch for where the *Turba Magna* <note>Latin: "The Great Turmoil" or "Great Wrath"; the point where natural or divine order breaks down into chaos or judgment.</note> is ignited in wrath, and there he is busy only as far as that turmoil reaches; beyond that, his courage is cooled.

Christ would only have had to let his desire enter into it and introduce his will into the Devil's. ## CHAPTER XI.

### *Of the process of Christ in his suffering, death, and Resurrection: Of the wonder of the sixth kingdom in the Mother of all Beings: How "It is finished" <note>original: "Consummatum est"</note> was accomplished, and how it is also symbolically achieved in the alchemical process.*

1. This is now to be considered: we must know that the essence of this world, along with man, consists of two properties: namely, Fire and Light, which are Love and Anger. Now the Fire is twofold, and the Light

<meta>This page continues Chapter 11, exploring the dual nature of fire and light within the alchemical and spiritual framework. # The Signature of All Things. Chapter 11.

[Mercury] is also twofold: a cold fire from the contraction <note>original: "Impression"</note> and a hot fire from the sphere <note>original: "Speer"</note> of *Mercury* within *Sulphur*. Similarly, there is a cold light from the cold fire and a warming light from the hot fire. The cold light is deceptive, while the hot light is good. This is not because the cold light is false in its own nature, but because within the contraction of the cold *Sulphur* and the sharpness of wrath, it turns into a false desire—that is, a false or selfish love which is contrary to meekness. Its desire is centered in *Saturn* and *Mars*.

<margin>It freely loses itself in the Nothing.</margin>
2. It puts forth its Sun (meaning its radiance of life) in *Mars*. The warming light—which also gains its fiery sharpness through the contraction within *Sulphur* from *Mars*—brings its desire back into freedom <note>original: "liberty"</note> by "dying" in the fire through anguish. It completely and freely gives itself up in the dying of the fire, abandoning the nature of wrath.

3. In this way, it becomes a universal joy rather than just its own, just like the sun that gives its shining radiance to everyone. Sunlight itself is neither hot nor cold; rather, *Mercury* within the Spirit of the Macrocosm <note>original: "great World"</note> creates heat within the properties of *Mars* and *Saturn*. The sun ignites their desire, making them grow hungry, eager, and active. Because of this, a fire is found within the light. This heat does not come from the light's own nature, but from the Soul of the Great Word <note>The Logos or creative speech of God</note>, which sharpens the pleasant light so intensely that it becomes unbearable to the eye.

4. We must carefully consider that if another "fire-desire"—one unlike the outward life of *Mercury*—tried to rule within the harsh wrath of outward Nature, it would be seen as an enemy to that cold, bitter, and fiery life. These forces would intensify <note>original: "exalt or exasperate"</note> their wrath, desperately wanting to be rid of it. This is exactly what happened when the Divine Love-desire manifested itself with great meekness to the false, cold, proud, and harsh fire-desire of those dominated by *Saturn*, *Mars*, and especially the false *Mercury*. It was a source of great opposition and enmity to them that Love should rule within the "death of poison" and live there. They could not and would not endure it, for Heaven had entered Hell to overcome Hell with Love and strip away its power. This is seen in the person of Christ: he loved them, did all kinds of good, and healed their diseases <note>original: "plagues"</note>. However, because he did not arise from their own wrathful power, and because he said he descended from above and was God’s Son, his presence was distasteful to the power of the cold and hot fires. They could not accept that he should rule over them with Love.

5. It is the same in the Philosophical Work <note>original: "Philosophick Work"; here referring to the alchemical process of the Great Work or *Magnum Opus*.</note>: when the wrathful forms of the earthly nature—namely, the outward *Saturn*, *Mars*, and *Mercury*—see the heavenly champion with the Virgin's property <note>In Boehme’s mysticism, the "Virgin" refers to Divine Wisdom or the Sophia-property.</note> among them, and perceive that he has a far different desire than they do, they become angry within themselves. For the love-desire, when it glimpses the fire-flash <note>original: "Fire-flagrat," from the Latin *flagrare* (to burn); it refers to a sudden, intense ignition or outburst of fire.</note>, awakens their own fire-flash. Then, the wrath proceeds from anxiety into Love, from which arises a death-flash within the Love. But since there can be no death within Love, the Love descends into the fire-flash and gives itself forth (or diffuses itself) into their desire, leaving its essence there. Thus, in their desire, they reach for its property within the death-flash. This is a poison to Death and a pestilence to Hell <note>A reference to Hosea 13:14: "O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction."</note>. In this property, Death was deprived of its power over humanity. For when Christ shed his heavenly blood in the flash of death and left it there, the wrath of God was compelled to retain the heavenly love-essence within itself. Right there, the fire-desire in ignited humanity was changed into a love-desire, and from the anguish of death † proceeded a joy and strength of Divine Power.

6. But I will give the well-wisher <note>Boehme’s term for a seeker of truth or a dedicated student.</note> a fundamental understanding of how it went with Christ, and how it goes in the same way with the Philosophical Work; both follow exactly the same process. Christ overcame the wrath of death in human nature <note>original: "Humane property," the inherent qualities of being human.</note> and changed the Father's anger into Love within human nature. The philosopher <note>The alchemist.</note> likewise has exactly such a will: he wants to turn the wrathful earth into heaven and change the poisonous *Mercury* into Love. Therefore, pay close attention: we will not write in parables here, but as clearly as sunshine.

7. God intended to change humanity back into the divine, heavenly state—after it had become earthly and had awakened the poisonous *Mercury* within the love-nature, which then devoured that love and transformed it into itself. He intended to make Heaven out of the human "earth," turning the four elements into only one, unified in *one desire*, and changing God's wrath within human nature into Love.

8. Now His anger was a power of fire and wrath ignited within man; therefore, it required true earnestness to withstand it and change it back into Love. Love had to enter into the Anger and give itself up entirely to the Wrath. It would not have been enough for God to remain in Heaven and only look upon humanity with love <note>original: "aspect," a term from astrology referring to the way planets influence each other from a distance.</note>; that alone could not have caused the anger and wrath to yield their power.

<summary>Boehme describes how the alchemical transformation of base materials mirrors the spiritual transformation of humanity, where divine Love must "die" into the wrathful properties of nature to overcome death and poison. He argues that this process of redemption is not a distant act of God but a physical and spiritual immersion into the "fire" of existence.</summary>

Understand that "the serpent" is the wrath of God in corrupted man, and its "head" is the power of God's anger. The divine man—meaning the divine property—was to change the earthly into itself and turn earth to heaven.

the Name *Jesus* in Divine Love and Heavenly essence <note>original: "essentiality"</note> must wholly surrender itself to be consumed by the Anger [of God]. The Son had to be, and was, obedient to the Angry Father, even to the death on the *Cross*, as the Scripture says.

19. Thus *Mercury* is annoyed by the child *Venus*, for *Venus* has completely revealed herself and freely surrendered. Now they may do whatever they wish; she will even go into the Dragon’s mouth—he only needs to open his jaws. *Mars* (acting within *Mercury*) does not understand this. Instead, they take the beautiful child and fire their poisonous arrows <note>original: "Darts"</note> against it, binding it with the power of *Saturn* in their wicked chains. The alchemist will see how they surround the color of *Venus*.

20. *Mars* brings it first to *Mercury*, since Mercury is the life-force. This is like [bringing Christ] before the High Priest, who must examine and test the beautiful child. But the High Priest hates it; he cannot reach into the heart to understand its Love-will. He only judges it by its outward appearance, because it does not share his nature <note>original: "property"</note>. It stands there with the same outward form as *Mercury* himself, yet it possesses a different Power, Virtue, and Will.

21. But because there is another **Mercury** which lives in its Love within the Child **Venus**, he cannot kill it. Instead, he brings it to **Saturn**, just as the **Jews** brought **Christ** from **Caiaphas** to **Pilate**. Pilate signifies Saturn, who also takes custody of the Child. The alchemist will then see the Child appear in his own form, looking as if he were covered in streaks from the poisonous rays of Mercury and Mars, which they press upon the Child through the influence of Saturn—just as Pilate had Jesus whipped. The alchemist will see the sharp crown of thorns pressing down upon the nature of the Child. He will also see that Venus does not move at all, but remains still and allows this to be done to her.

24. Furthermore, we must understand how **Adam** had taken on a cold, false love, and presented himself before God as if he possessed his own power and will, and were God's child. In reality, he was only mocking God, for that is how the desire for love appears when it is imprisoned in the "impression" or "contraction" of death.

25. In this way, the second **Adam**, **Christ**, had to take all of this upon himself. If the Child would only contribute the power of the "Fire’s Center"—the Divine might—then it would be like the Sun and would be a lord over the **Sulphur** <note>the essential substance or "burning" quality</note> of Mars and Mercury. ...namely, the divine and human aspects divide themselves within the form of each power. The Artist <note>the alchemist or spiritual seeker</note> may see this if he has the eyes and understanding for it.

Love also stands in the source of the wrath during the "flash" <note>original: "flagrat"; in Boehme’s philosophy, this is a sudden ignition or stroke of spiritual energy or light</note> of death, appearing powerless (or in a faint). It gives itself up entirely to the stroke of death, and in that moment, the heavenly essence—the heavenly blood—flows from it into the property of the third principle <note>the material world or the human soul</note>, represented by the **Young Man**. Here, the **Virgin** <note>representing Divine Wisdom or Sophia</note> gives her "Pearl" <note>the spiritual treasure or soul-essence</note> to the Young Man as his own property, and God and man become one.

35. For the Virgin’s blood, coming from the divine essence, now drowns the Young Man’s blood—his self-centered nature <note>original: "Self hood"</note>—with its essence of Love. The "three murderers" <note>Saturn, Mars, and Mercury in their corrupted, wrathful states</note> surrender their lives in the Virgin’s blood. Then the red glow <note>original: "glee"</note> from the Fire and the white glow from the life of the **Champion** <note>the conquering spirit of Christ</note> rise up together: life arises from the wrath, and meekness from the Love. Both the life of anger and the life of love ascend together as a single life, for in death they become one. Death dies away in Love and becomes the life of the divine kingdom of joy. This is not a destruction <note>original: "dying"</note>, but a free surrender of its power, might, and will—a **transmutation**. The Virgin’s blood changes the human nature (which was dead toward God) into heavenly blood. The life of the Young Man dies, and the life of the Deity remains fixed and steadfast, for it stands in its own property within the **Nothing** <note>the *Ungrund*, or the divine source beyond all being and differentiation</note>.

36. You have found a treasure in this valley of misery that surpasses the value of gold. Take it and value it as more excellent and sovereign than anything else that shall rise from death. If you are born of God, you will understand my meaning.

...exemplified it. It is not a mere verbal forgiveness, as "Babel" <note>original: "Babel"; Boehme's term for the confused, superficial institutional church</note> teaches. No, no—the human will must, with all its powers, enter into this death, into this blood—namely, into the Highest Tincture <note>the ultimate spiritual essence that transforms base matter into gold, or sin into holiness</note>.

38. The purple robe which Christ wore could not do it; the white, hypocritical, Pharisaical priest’s coat could also not achieve it. The crafty, malignant man <note>the old, sinful self</note> must be put to death <note>original: "mortified"</note> in Christ’s blood; he must be drowned in the Virgin’s blood. *The seed of the woman must bruise the head of the serpent.* The will must completely disclaim and depart from its own self-interest <note>original: "selfness"</note> and become as an innocent child, entering entirely into God’s mercy—into the virgin-like blood of Christ—so that sin and the poisoned Mercury <note>the restless, driving life-force</note> may be drowned in its Mars <note>the fiery, wrathful principle</note>, so that the white Lion may arise. For the Lion which now appears in white, and in crimson red, is the Mercury of life—that is, the "Expressed Word" <note>God's creative speech manifested in the soul</note> or the Soul. This soul was previously a wrathful devil in its self-centeredness <note>original: "self-hood"</note>, ruling and dominating in the anger of God within the three forms of the "poison-source": namely, in Saturn <note>the restrictive, hardening force</note>, Mars, and Mercury. Now it is the white, scarlet-colored Lion from the House of David and Israel, fulfilled in the Covenant of promise.

->NB.<-

39. But so that we may satisfy the "well-wisher" <note>the earnest seeker</note>, we will further show them the whole foundation, even up to the resurrection of Christ. When the Jews had hung Jesus upon the Cross, and He had shed His human and heavenly divine blood, and drowned the *Turba* <note>original: "Turba"; the principle of wrath, disruption, or chaotic destruction</note> in the human blood, then Jesus said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do."

40. When Jesus had broken Death within humanity and removed "Self," he did not then completely cast away the human property—the place where Death and the anger of God resided—but rather, he then truly took it up for the first time. Understand this: he even then truly took the outward kingdom into the inward. For the outward kingdom was born as a wonder out of the Eternal Wisdom in the "Speaking Word" <note>the creative utterance of God</note> and spoken forth into a form as a manifestation of the Deity in love and anger, in good and evil. So, Jesus did not want the outward type <note>the physical form</note> of these wonders—made in the likeness of God—to perish or completely vanish. Instead, he wanted the wrath, which had overpowered the love in man, to be forgiven. That is, it should be given into the "Nothing"—namely, into Liberty <note>the divine stillness or the "Ungrund" in Boehme's thought</note>—so that it might not be manifest in its own self-centered property. It must become a servant, and only a cause for fiery love and divine joyfulness. Nothing should perish or be lost in man, for God had created him in His own image.

41. Thus, let the philosopher observe that when the three murderers—namely, **Saturn**, **Mars**, and **Mercury**—† sink into the crimson-colored blood of the Lion, they do not perish.
