He transforms his mother, in whom he lay shut up in death, into **Sol**. He makes the earthly become heavenly in a single property, just as the Virgin was. Here, the Virgin loses her name, for she has given her love and her pearl to the Champion, who is now called the **white Lion**. This is as the Scripture speaks of the Lion of the House of Israel and David, who would demolish the Devil's kingdom and destroy Hell—that is, break the anger of God and change it into love.

43. This Champion or Lion is neither man nor woman, but he is both. The **tincture** <note>the spiritual essence that transforms nature</note> of the fire and the light must become one: namely, the essence, which is **Venus**, and the spirit, which is **Mars** within **Mercury**. The Father’s love and anger must become one thing, and then this one thing is called the kingdom of joy. So long as these are separated, there is nothing in the thing but anguish, torment, and mere desire; but when it burns in one will, it is a joyful proceeding forth from itself. This outgoing <note>original: "egressive"</note> property is called the **Holy Ghost**—the very life of the Deity.

44. Therefore, know that the blood of both the Virgin and the young man must be shed together so that the "fire-lion" might die. This fire-lion was manifested in the human property so that the love of the Virgin might change his wrath—in her dear love-blood—into her own property, and so obtain the soul from the young man. For in **Adam**, the Virgin disappeared, because the soul departed from its love-will and from its <term>resignation</term> <note>Boehme's term for the total surrender of the self-will to God's will</note> into its own self-interest, becoming disobedient to God.

They do not consider that the Mother is a widow, and that Christ has left and ordained them to be her caretakers <note>original: "Curates"</note>, just as John was.

60. O dear Mother of Christendom, let these wolves, bears, and lions go, and let them shelter themselves wherever they please; pay no more attention to these evil beasts. Embrace John, the disciple of Christ, who teaches love and humility.

61. O dear and worthy Mother, are you not the only one? Why do you allow the lions to rend and tear you to pieces? Christ is your husband; all these others are strangers and hirelings <note>Those who work for wages rather than out of true devotion.</note>, unless they walk in your childlike love and humble themselves toward the Mother, providing for her as ministers. Otherwise, they are all wolves, bears, and tearing lions. Even if there were many thousands of them, none is any better than the others unless he comes forward in the tradition of John and takes care of Christ’s Mother, providing for her with earnestness in Christ’s Spirit. If he does not have that Spirit, he is not called by Christ to be a guardian or caretaker of the Mother; instead, he is a Mercurialite—a Pharisee—the kind Christ called the "offspring of serpents" and "brood of vipers," who crucify Jesus in his members.

62. And so, the philosopher <note>The alchemist or seeker of divine wisdom.</note> must consider and carefully observe Christ's Mother, whom He entrusted to John’s care. He must likewise be a "John" and know that his business concerns the...

### The Signature of All Things. CHAPTER 12. <note>original: "Signatura Rerum. CHAP. II." Though the header says Chapter 2, it follows Chapter 12 in the text's progression.</note>

The rocks split apart, for Death was terrified by the Life. Here, the property of the awakened Wrath severed itself into the center—that is, into the First Principle, into the fire-root. Now, from that center, there proceeded a hunger for the New Birth in the human property; the hunger for Death was transformed into a hunger for Life, for Love infused <note>original: "tinctured." In alchemy, a tincture is a substance that transforms or purifies another.</note> the Anger, so that the fire-desire of the dark Impression <note>The "Impression" refers to the contracting, hardening force of material existence.</note> became a desire for Life.

68. Understand this correctly: God the Father, who gave his beloved Heart into humanity to help mankind, now thirsted for that humanity—that is, for his Heart or Word of Power. The Deity within humanity—the Heart of the Father—thirsted for the Father, and the essence of the Light thirsted for the essence of the Fire. For the soul’s essence in **Adam** had departed from the essential nature of Love (which constituted Paradise) into a state of self-centeredness <note>original: "Selfness."</note>, becoming disobedient to God. Because of this, the essence, life, and being of the Light and Love died in its growth; it withered in terms of its vegetative life—its heavenly growth, blooming, and the awareness of the Paradisiacal source—and instead woke up and arose into the earthly world.

69. Here, the Father brought the soul, which had entered into his Wrath and manifested itself in his Anger, back into Love—that is, back into the vanished image of Paradise. Here, the dark world was terrified in Death’s <term>Flagrat</term> <note>original: "Flagrat"; Böhme's term for a sudden, explosive flash or shattering shock of energy, like a lightning bolt, that marks a spiritual transition.</note> by the Fire-<term>Flagrat</term> which arose in Love within Death as a joyful shock. This joy-shock entered into the dead bodies of those in **Israel** who hoped for the **Messiah**, sounding like the power of God and awakening them from death.

70. This <term>Flagrat</term> tore the Veil of the Temple in two—that is, the **Veil of Moses**, which hung before the clear face of God so that man could not see Him. Because of that veil, man had to serve Him through offerings and symbolic rituals <note>original: "Type."</note> of this final discovery, in which God manifested Himself again in humanity. This <term>Flagrat</term> broke the symbolism of the offerings and sacrifices, revealed the clear face of God, and united human time with eternity.

71. Everything that the **Jews** did outwardly to **Christ** was a symbolic representation of the internal process—that is, how things proceeded between God and humanity, or between eternity and time. The **Jews** gave **Jesus** gall and vinegar in his thirst; both of these properties represent **Mercury** within the **Sulphur** of **Saturn**—that is, within the "Impression." This is a perfect resemblance of the soul's property as it exists by itself, entirely devoid of the other properties of Love.

# THE SIGNATURE OF ALL THINGS. CHAPTER 12. <note>original: "CHAP. II. Signatura Rerum." As noted on the previous page, while the header says Chapter 2, it is part of the sequence of Chapter 12.</note>

72. God returned this property of the Soul back into His Love—death into life. He brought the vanished essence of Love (which the Word of God had taken upon itself in the essence and seed of **Mary**, and brought to life) into the property of Wrath <note>original: "Angers property."</note>—into the soul's essence, namely, into the center of the Fire and the dark world. Because of this, the soul-like Fire and the dark world became an exceedingly triumphant, joyful, paradisiacal life. Here, the Champion <note>Refers to Christ.</note> rebuked Death and Hell—that is, the dark world within the soul—and said: *Death! Where is your sting now in man? Hell! Where is now your victory in the poison-source in the expressed Word or Mercury?* <note>In Boehme's alchemy, "Mercury" represents the dynamic, communicative power of the divine Word as it acts upon nature.</note> All is now dead. O Death, I am your death! Hell, I am your conqueror! You must serve me for the Kingdom of Joy; you shall be my servant and minister to the Kingdom of Joy. You shall ignite the flames of Love with your wrath and be the cause of the spring in Paradise.

73. In this way, we give the Philosopher <note>likely referring to an alchemist or "natural philosopher."</note> to understand our meaning and profound foundation in Nature. He who desires to seek and open the vanished essence of the Earth—which lies locked up in death, namely, in the curse of God—must realize that the Veil of **Moses** <note>A biblical metaphor for the spiritual blindness that prevents one from seeing the true reality behind the physical world.</note> also hangs before him. A very sincere earnestness is required to tear that veil in two so that he may be able to see the face of Nature; otherwise, he is not fit for the task.

74. And just as it happened in the humanity of Christ, between God’s Love and Wrath, where both were transformed into one: so it is in his Work of Nature. The poisonous *Mercury* in the *Sulfur* <note>In alchemy, Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt are the three primary substances (Tria Prima). Sulfur often represents the soul or the combustible principle.</note> of *Mars* and *Saturn* gives its *Lunar Menstruum* <note>original: "Menstruum." In alchemy, a solvent or base fluid. "Lunar" suggests a silver or cooling property.</note>—which is the greatest poison of the dark source—into the property of *Venus*. When *Venus* thirsts for the Fire of Love, then *Mercury* pours its poison into the thirst of *Venus*. *Venus’s* thirst then gives itself entirely to the poison, as if it died; it wholly yields up its desiring life. Upon this, a great darkness arises in the Philosophical Work; for the matter <note>original: "Materia."</note> becomes as black as a raven, because *Venus* has resigned its life, from which the radiance [or splendor] arises. This can be seen in the example of Christ, when the sun lost its light and there was a great darkness, contrary to the common course of nature.

75. For when the internal Sun surrendered itself to the Wrath—that is, into the darkness of God—then the external sun (which receives its power and luster from the internal, as a mirror or image of the internal) could not shine. This was because its root, from which it shines, had entered into the darkness in the place of this world. It intended to turn the darkness in the curse of God into light; namely, it would make the place of this world Paradise once again.

Again, the forty hours Christ spent in the Grave correspond to the forty days **Adam** spent in Paradise, the forty days **Moses** spent on the Mount, the forty years in the wilderness, and the forty days after the Resurrection before the Ascension; they are all one and the same. Now, when the Champion had endured **Adam’s** trial, the soul was tempted for forty days in its human property to see whether it would eat of **God’s Word** and live in full, resigned obedience to the **Will of God**. Thus, the substance stands once again in the beginning, in the order God created. It must only remain in its "impression" within the Word of Creation <note>original: "Verbum Fiat"; Latin for "Let it be done"</note>—that is, in the divine making—until the day of God’s separation, when God will change time back into eternity.

Then the whole man, Christ, said: *“My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?”* For God’s Speaking Word was now silent within His human nature. 88. Here, Love destroyed death and opened the tight seal, so that the will might again enter into what it was before it became a creature. Thus the created self-will dies; it enters wholly into the *Nothing* <note>The "Ungrund" or the absolute freedom beyond all nature and essence</note>, so that it might no longer live for itself, but for God.

## CHAPTER XII.

->*Concerning the seventh form in the Kingdom of the Mother: how the seventh kingdom—namely, the Kingdom of the Sun—is opened again and made alive, explained through the parable or likeness of Christ’s resurrection.*<-

<margin>* The created soul.</margin>
1. We must not think that when Christ died the natural death in his human nature <note>original: "Humane property"</note>, he died in regards to his * created soul, much less in regards to his divinity. Furthermore, he did not disappear or die in his heavenly substance <note>original: "Heavenly Essentiality"</note> or in the heavenly Tincture <note>original: "Heavenly Tincture"; a spiritual "dye" or quality that transforms and glorifies matter</note>; this would be impossible. Rather, he only gave the will and dominion of the "Self"—that is, the influence of the outward world which dominated humanity and led to the self-centered will and powers of the selfish creature (in which humanity was disobedient to God)—entirely into the Father's hands. He surrendered it into the "end of nature," into the Father’s Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"; the chaos or potential from which God creates</note>. This was not so that it should be dead, but so that God's Spirit alone might be its life, and that divine dominion might exist in Christ's person. In this way, the eternal Father might rule and reign with his eternal Spirit in his own image. Therefore, God has determined to conduct the Last Judgment through this Jesus.

2. Now, the human nature <note>original: "Creature"</note> of Christ does not do this alone, but God does it within his own image, through that human nature, in the dominion of his...

...the Eternal Spirit of all three principles <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Three Principles" are the Dark World (God's anger/fire), the Light World (God's love/light), and the Outer World (the physical universe)</note>, which is the life and dominion of every being, existing in each thing according to its specific nature.

3. And understand us correctly: when Christ died on the Cross, the name *Jesus*—which destroyed Death and tinctured <term>Tincture: A spiritual life-force that heals or transforms a substance into a higher state.</term> the expressed Word <note>original: "expressed Word"; the Word of God as it is manifested in physical creation</note>, namely the form of the Godhead (or the "Formed Word"), specifically the soul, with love—did not also die. No, it cannot be; Eternity does not die. Only the spoken word [dies], which stands again in the desire of the Speaking [Word], namely in the *Fiat* <note>Latin: "let it be done"; the creative command of God</note>, which changes itself in its own speaking—that is, in its self-desire. It brings its own sound into a different form and source than the Speaking Word had originally spoken it and set it forth with the *Verbum Fiat* <note>original: "Verbum Fiat"; Latin for "The Word of the Fiat"</note> into a form, signature <note>The outward appearance that reveals the inner spiritual character</note>, and will. This is what *Lucifer* did with his royal throne, and what *Adam* also did, when they both departed from surrender <note>original: "Resignation"; the act of yielding one's self-will to God</note> into selfhood; the instrument wanted to be the master.

4. The outward-working sensory life, in which the anger of God was ignited, died away completely—not so that it should become *nothing*, but it fell into the "Nothing," namely into God’s will, into God’s working and feeling. It moved entirely away from the will of the outward world (which is both evil and good), so that it might no longer live for the world—that is, for the *Astrum* <note>The "star" or astral influence that governs physical and emotional life</note> in the heat <note>original: "walm"; a bubbling or surging energy</note> of the four elements—but rather for the Eternal Father’s nature in the surging heat of the pure divine element. The life of the outward world died.

5. Thus, the true human life immediately fell back into that place from which *Adam* had brought it, namely into *Paradise*. Whereupon Christ said to the thief, *Today you shall be with me in Paradise* <note>Luke 23:43</note>. It fell into *Adam’s* death—the death by which he died to Paradise—and sprouted up within *Adam’s* death as a new creature out of the old, just as a branch sprouts from a grain of corn. And it did this by the might and power of the Speaking Word, which out of grace had entered with living substance into the faded heavenly essence of man. It had freely given itself into the center of the soul’s nature and also into the wrath of the anger and death in the flesh; it changed that anger into love and tinctured the corrupt blood within the anger with that love.

6. The divine tincture <note>A transformative spiritual force</note> influenced the human one; the divine Sun entered into the human sun. The divine Sun entered into *Adam’s* night, namely into *Adam’s* sleep <note>Böhme views the "sleep" of Adam as his fall from divine consciousness into the illusions of the material world</note>. God’s Sun, through the name *Jesus*, entered with *Adam’s* soul and humanity—within the person of Christ—into death, which is to say, into *Adam’s* sleep.

The self-will and its hunger are dead and absorbed into the "Nothing," and the *Lubet* of eternal liberty is now its life. Now, seeing that the Highest Being once moved itself and entered into a visible, understandable essence, it again forms that same essence. This essence departs from its selfhood and enters into the "Nothing," returning to the kind of being it was before the world began. But seeing that the **Word: "Let there be"** <note>original: *Verbum Fiat*; the creative command of God in Genesis.</note> still stands to this day, creating the physical essence, it again creates a fixed, perfect essence. The same thing is accomplished in the Alchemical Work <note>original: "Philosophick Work"; the process of creating the "Philosopher's Stone" or achieving spiritual perfection.</note>, where a new life arises out of death, just as God raises us up in Himself through Christ, if we die to our selfhood and wholly resign ourselves to Him.

...the creative <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be done," referring to God’s command at creation.</note>, and they belong to God’s activity on the final day of Separation (at this time for his own manifestation, his honor, and his wondrous deeds). But after this time, they belong to the crystalline world in the "sea of glass" before the Ancient of Days in the <note>original: "Apocalyps"; the Book of Revelation.</note> Apocalypse.

### ->A Brief Summary of the Philosophical WORK.<-

29. Our meaning might seem very difficult to the reader because we take such a long way around and show Christ throughout the process. Let no one wonder at this; we do not seek gold or any temporal goods by this, nor do we wish to drive people into vain curiosities. We speak only to the "children" whom God has chosen for this purpose. For the time is now born when that which was lost shall be found again—not only the Universal <note>The "Universal" or *Universal Medicine* was the alchemical goal of a substance that could cure all diseases and perfect all metals.</note> for the body of this world, but also for the soul.

30. The process is very short in both cases, and it involves only one property, which is this: the Tree (meaning the Life) is divided into seven forms <note>Boehme’s "Seven Forms of Nature" describe the progression of spiritual qualities from dark, restrictive desire to light and divine expression.</note>. Now, God’s curse has entered into these seven forms so that they are in strife and enmity; one form annoys the other, and they can never agree unless all seven enter into death and die to their own self-will. Now, this cannot happen unless a "Death" enters them to break their will and be a death unto them—just as the Deity in Christ was a death to human self-hood and the seven forms in human life. It is the same here: the human will in Christ was changed into the Eternal Sun—namely, into <term>resignation</term> <note>original: "Resignation"; in Boehme's theology, this is 'Gelassenheit,' the act of yielding one's ego and will to God.</note> in God. Even so, all the forms in the philosophical work must be changed into one, namely into <term>Sol</term> <note>Latin for "Sun"; in alchemy, it represents gold and spiritual perfection, often symbolizing the light of Christ.</note>. The seven must become one, yet remain as seven, but with one desire where each form desires the other in love; then there is no more strife or contest.

<margin>† It creates itself, or it has its own maker <note>original: "faber"; Latin for craftsman or smith.</note> within itself.</margin>
31. Therefore, let the practitioner <note>original: "Artist"; the seeker or alchemist performing the work.</note> consider how he may put death to death using the pure life, and how he may awaken the dead and vanished life—which is heavenly and lies hidden and imprisoned within the Curse—so that it may receive the fire-soul <note>The "fire-soul" represents the core of human consciousness and desire that needs to be enlightened.</note> once again. If he brings it this far, it † works of its own accord.

32. When the Virgin <note>Often referring to "Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, the spiritual counterpart to the soul.</note> again receives her bridegroom who has been unfaithful, then he is prepared and fitted for the work; otherwise, he is not fit at all, and everything he attempts is in vain and to no purpose. There is no possibility for the heavenly image (made in God’s likeness in man) to be otherwise helped and restored after the fire-soul had entered

# The Signature of All Things <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"; Latin title of the work.</note>. CHAPTER 12.

...into its selfhood, unless the Spirit of God introduced itself into the disappeared Image—namely, into the Heavenly Essentiality <note>The "Heavenly Essentiality" refers to the spiritual substance or "body" of heaven that was lost at the Fall.</note>—and gave itself, along with that same Image awakened within it, into the Soul's Fire (the wrath of Death). This was done to be a "death to Death"—namely, to the wrathful anger of God—so that it might be drowned in Love, in the blood of the Heavenly Essentiality. And although there could be no parting or dying of the soul itself, yet there was a "dying" of the Wrath, so that the Wrath was changed into joy and Love.

33. In exactly the same way, the Artist’s Work <note>The "Artist" refers to the alchemist or spiritual practitioner performing the "Great Work."</note> proceeds in no other fashion. For Man was created out of all Beings, out of Heaven and Earth; but when he became wholly earthly and the Curse seized him, the Curse also came over the earthly Being from which Man was made. Thus, Heaven was shut up from man, and Heaven was also shut up in the Earth—in metals, trees, and herbs, in the food of Man, and in whatever belonged to his ornament and delight.

<margin>Derived from.</margin>
34. The soul of the Earth—namely, the property of the Fire of the first Principle <note>The "first Principle" in Boehme's system represents the dark, consuming fire of God's power/wrath before it is transmuted into light.</note>—has entered into its own selfhood, which is God's anger. Now, Heaven is hidden within it; therefore, the Artist in his work must reduce the Soul in the Curse and the Heaven back into One. He must introduce the Soul again into Heaven, or else there is no possibility of success. Now, he cannot bring the Soul in its iniquity into Heaven, for it will not go. Therefore, he must bring Heaven into the Soul and wholly give Heaven into the Soul, so that the Soul may "eat" of Heaven, whether she wants to or not. 
<margin>Or, as if dead.</margin>
Heaven must be as if dead in the Soul, so that the Soul cannot get rid of it, no matter how angry she may be or how vehemently she rages against it, until she is overcome in her wrath and enters with her Desire into Heaven (the disappeared Essence). There, she wills to murder it, just as the Jews murdered Christ. And if she thus enters into the Heavenly Essence, then the Image of the Heavenly Essence falls into the jaws of the Murderer.

35. Thus, when the Heavenly Essence gives its desire unto the Murderer, the Murderer is dismayed at the precious Love-life and arises in the "Flagrat" <note>original: "Flagrat"; a term Boehme uses for a sudden flash, shock, or discharge of energy that marks the turning point from darkness/wrath to light/love.</note>—the dismayment—within the Heavenly Essentiality. Thus, the disappeared Essence receives the Fire-Flagrat back into itself and wholly unites itself with the Fire-life. So, the Fire must burn in Love and Meekness and 
<margin>Or, abandon its right.</margin>
abandon its right in the Center, just as the Light shines from the Fire. In this way, and no other, the Heavenly Essence obtains its life. Just as a fire heats through a piece of iron so that it appears as if it were mere fire—and it is so, yet the iron still retains its substance—even so the disappeared Essence...

# THE SIGNATURE OF ALL THINGS <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"; Latin title of the work.</note>. CHAPTER 12.

...Heaven is revealed in the poisonous Mercurial <note>original: "Mercurial"; referring to the quick, volatile, and often unstable principle associated with the planet Mercury.</note> and Martial <note>original: "Martial"; referring to the aggressive, fiery principle associated with the planet Mars.</note> fire-soul, making only one Will out of seven; yet the seven remain, but the conflict <note>original: "Enmity"</note> stops.

<margin>Opposition <note>original: "Contra-will"</note>.</margin>
36. This is a "Universal" <note>An alchemical term for a medicine or substance believed to be capable of curing all diseases or transforming all matter into its highest state.</note> which also changes the conflict or harmful nature <note>original: "Malignity"</note> of all diseases in the human body into one single Will [into unity]. In this way, the raging and raving—namely, the seven forms of life in their conflict—become harmonious; then the hunger of the disease stops, and the process to the Universal continues as has been already mentioned. It is not my intention to provide a clearer explanation of this; it is already clear enough. Anyone who does not seek to become a "new man born in God" and apply themselves diligently to it should not meddle with my writings.

37. I have not written anything for that kind of seeker, and they will not be able to fundamentally understand our meaning—no matter how much they try—unless they enter into a state of surrender <note>original: "Resignation"; a key concept in Boehme's theology referring to the total surrender of the self-will to God's will.</note> in Christ. Only there can one grasp the Spirit of the Universal; otherwise, everything is pointless. We faithfully warn the curious critic not to waste their time, for they will achieve nothing this way unless they enter into it themselves. Then it will be shown to them without much searching, for the way is childlike [plain and easy].

### CHAPTER XIII.

<margin>† Conflict, contrariety.</margin>
->On the Conflict of the Spirit and the Body, and on their Cure and Remedy.<-

<margin>Or, signs and marks itself in the body.</margin>
1. Every body is in itself a senseless and dead thing or being; it is only a manifestation of the spirit that is within it. The spirit is marked upon the body. Whatever the spirit is in its own imperceptible <note>original: "incomprehensible"</note> operation, the body is the same in a perceptible and visible way. One of the seven forms of nature is superior and chief; the others are attached to it and give their "signs" as well, depending on how strong each one is in its essence. Just as the forms are ordered in each thing, they "sign" <note>To "sign" or "signature" here refers to the outward physical marks or characteristics that reveal the inner spiritual nature of a thing.</note> the body of every thing and creature in its generation [or kind]. This is the manifestation of Divine Wisdom in the expressed Word of Love and Anger.

2. There is nothing that does not have its soul within it according to its specific nature, and the soul is like a kernel for another body. Everything that lives and grows has its seed within it. God has contained <note>original: "comprehended"</note> all things in His Word and spoken them into a form, just as the Will had † conceived <margin>† Or, contained, or conceived.</margin> itself within the Desire. That which is expressed [or spoken] is a blueprint <note>original: "Plat-form"</note> of the Speaking, and it contains the Speaking within it once again. This same Speaking is a seed for another image according to the first; for both work together: namely, the Speaking and the Spoken [Word].

<margin>
* Colors of distinction.
ᵃ Element.
† Or, Clock/Watch.
</margin>
3. The Speaking works within itself—that is, in Eternity—and the Spoken also works within itself—that is, in Time. The Speaking is the Master, and the Spoken is the instrument. The Speaking creates the nature of Eternity, and the Spoken creates the nature of Time. Each creates two properties within its own scope: Light and Darkness, in which the fundamental element <margin>ᵃ Element.</margin> of all beings consists. In the Expressed Word, this element divides itself into the four elements [fire, air, water, earth], but in the Speaking Word, there is only one. The element in itself is neither hot nor cold, nor dry nor moist; rather, it is a *Lubet* <term>Lubet: From the Latin 'libitum,' meaning a longing, delight, or the first movement of the will toward expression.</term>—a desiring will—in which the Divine Wisdom creates the * various colors and distinctions <margin>* Colors of distinction.</margin>, all according to the nature of the Desire. In this element, there is neither number nor end, but in the four elements, there are both numbers and endings. For by being expressed (in that they have become self-contained), they have taken a beginning and formed themselves into a model or blueprint of time, which runs like a † clock <margin>† Or, Clock/Watch <note>original: "Horologue"</note>.</margin>; it forms, shapes, and destroys.

4. This clockwork consists of seven forms or properties (as mentioned before), which create within themselves a three-fold spirit: namely, a vegetative [growth], sensitive [feeling], and rational [reasoning] spirit. The vegetative spirit consists of the four elements; the sensitive spirit consists of the seven forms of nature; and the rational spirit consists of the constellation <note>original: "Constellation"; referring to the cosmic and astrological influences believed to shape the human mind and temperament.</note>. However, true understanding proceeds only from God, for it arises out of Eternal Nature. All life, whatever its kind, that has its limits within the Expressed Word, consists of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury <note>original: "Sal, Sulphur, and Mercury"; the "Tria Prima" or three primary substances of alchemy, representing the body, soul, and spirit of all matter.</note>; for within these consist the seven properties of every life in this world, as well as the spirits of growth, sensation, and reason.

5. Sulfur is the mother of all spirituality and physicality. Mercury manages the rule within it, and Salt is the house where it lives, which Mercury itself builds within Sulfur. Reason arises in the oil <note>original: "Oyl"</note> of the Sulfur, into which the constellation gives its desire—that is, the essence of its specific nature.

By this cure, we may heal ourselves in our own "Self-hood" <note>Self-hood: The state of being focused on one's own ego or fallen nature.</note> and bring ourselves into the * limit of rest.

7. We will describe and declare this, if there is anyone who has a mind to enter upon it and truly prove and try it. We will set forth how evil and good arise originally, and how they arise to give the understanding researcher the opportunity to seek. We will show how the will toward evil and good arises, and how evil is the death of the good, and conversely, how the good is the death of the evil.

8. When we consider what the *Mercurial* life is, we find that it consists of *Sulphur* <term>Sulphur: To Böhme, this represents the "burning" desire or the fundamental energy of a being.</term>. For *Sulphur* is a dry hunger for matter, which creates an "austere impression" <note>austere impression: A drawing-inward or contraction that creates density and harshness.</note>. In its austere impression, it contains the Fire, and also the Oil from which the life burns. Now, this "impression" creates coldness, and its conjunction or contraction creates heat; † so that now there is a cold fire and a hot fire in one thing. The cold creates within itself hardness and darkness, and the heat creates within itself the light. Yet there could be no light if the Oil in the *Sulphur* did not die in fervent, hot anguish, just as a candle dies as it burns in the fire.

9. Now, there is a two-fold "dying" in *Sulphur*, from which a two-fold life is also generated. First, the impression or desire draws in, contracts, encloses, and makes things hard, cold, and thick. This hardness—namely, the enclosed state—causes a death in the enclosed being. Yet, in that spirit, there is no true death, but rather a stinging, raging, and anxious "cold fire-life," which is generated along with the impression and is the life of the darkness.

10. Secondly, in that same anguish and austere desire, the hot fire is generated. This fire consumes the substance created by the coldness (namely, the impression of the desire toward nature). Thus, there remains a conflict in the fire between the cold and the heat. The cold wants to have its life according to its own property, and because it strives for life, it kindles the heat in its impression, and forthwith the...

10. The heat deprives the cold of its power and consumes the cold's substance; then also the fire-spirit cannot survive, for unless it has substance, it goes out. Therefore, it must continually and without stopping die within itself in the fiery, anxious desire. As long as it has the cold's substance to live upon, its life arises, and yet it is nothing but a constant dying and consuming; in its act of devouring <note>original: "Devoration"</note> is the greatest hunger for substance. This same hunger passes through and with the devouring out of the fire's dying and dwells in the Nothing. Yet it may not be a *Nothing*, and also it cannot be a Nothing; therefore, it draws the fire again into itself, for its own desire is turned toward its Mother. But because it has once died to the fire-source <term>fire-source: Böhme often uses "source" or "quality" (German: Qual) to describe the driving, often painful energy of a thing.</term>, it cannot die any more in the fire of the heat or cold. Instead, it continually proceeds forth from the fire, and the fire draws it again continually into itself, and so it is the life of the fire. This is the **Air**, which in the fire is rightly called **Wind** because of its strength and force; and in that * which has proceeded forth, it is properly called **Air** because of its life of gentleness <note>original: "meekness"</note>.

11. And in the dying of the fire, we are to understand the **Oil** <note>original: "Oyl"</note>, from which the fire receives its shining light, in which the true life is understood. For that which proceeds forth in the fire-death with the desire to be delivered and freed from the fire-source is a desire of gentleness; it takes its origin in the first Will to Nature, in which the Eternal Nothing brings itself into a desire through its *Lubet* <term>Lubet: From the Latin 'libitum,' meaning a longing, delight, or the first movement of the divine will toward manifestation.</term>.

12. This *Lubet* brings itself forth through the cold and hot death (through both types of dying) again into liberty—namely, into the **NOTHING**. Thus, it is manifested in the harsh <note>original: "Austere"</note> impression through the fire and brought into a principle; yet it is not made of either the fire or the cold, though that is how it is manifested.

13. But since the Eternal *Lubet* to Nature introduces itself into a desire along with Nature, this desire cannot die in either the cold or heat; for it takes its origin neither in the heat nor the cold, but in the Nothing. And so it is that after it proceeds forth from the dying in the fire, it is again desiring—namely, of its own property—and it impresses <term>impresses: To draw inward, contract, or give form to substance.</term> itself, for in the fire it has taken the impression.

# Signatura Rerum. CHAP. 13.

19. [The three]-fold wheel <note>The text begins mid-sentence; based on Böhme's philosophy, this likely refers to the "three-fold wheel" of the divine essence</note> is the first explanation [or working forth] of the Chaos and creates the second body, namely: Reason. The second body reveals the first and is also a spiritual body; the third body is elemental—a cabinet or container for both the first two—and is a visible, tangible body.

20. The first body—namely the Chaos, or the first <margin>Constellation</margin> constellation—is the Word expressed out of the Eternal Conception, because it is spiritual. This Word has its own "speaking" within itself, which is the <term>mercurial wheel</term> <note>original: "Mercurial Wheel"; in Böhme's thought, this represents the dynamic, moving spirit of life and circulation</note> within the <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "Sulphur"; representing the underlying substance or "soul-fire" of a thing</note> with its seven forms. This, in turn, speaks forth from itself the four elements.

21. Thus, one proceeds from the other. The very first thing, existing before the Chaos, is the <term>Lubet</term> <note>original: "Lubet"; from the German "Lust," meaning a joyful inclination, divine "good pleasure," or longing</note> of Eternity in the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: "Abyss"; the "Ungrund," or the bottomless, groundless void of the divine essence</note>, which takes within itself a will toward its own manifestation. This is entirely God. This Will conceives a desire within the Lubet; this is the Chaos, or the first <term>Astrum</term> <note>original: "Astrum"; star or celestial influence</note>, in which Eternal Nature consists. With this desire toward nature, it introduces itself into seven forms (as mentioned before) and thus manifests the Chaos—namely, the eternal hidden wisdom of God. Through the desire in the mercurial wheel, the "Element" is formed, which is a spiritual body of the mercurial life.

22. Now, all of this is twofold: the Desire creates darkness within itself through its <term>impression</term> <note>original: "Impression"; the spiritual act of contracting or compressing toward a center</note>, where the strong power of nature’s ignition lies, and it is painful. Conversely, the free Lubet, acting upon the Desire, creates a light and pleasing motion through that same ignition. The Light is the power and brilliance, and the "Element" is its body or essence, though at this stage it is still only spiritual. Thus, the "fire-desire" is a state of joyfulness within the free Lubet, but in the darkness, it is an aching, painful source.

23. Out of this whole essence, Man was created in the image of God. Understand us correctly: after and during creation, he lived under the dominion of the spiritual Element. The <margin>Sphere</margin> mercurial wheel in sulfur stood in the Light and in the free Lubet of Eternity. However, he wandered further away with his desire into the four material elements—namely, into the center of darkness in creation, from which heat and cold arise.

24. In the beginning, his desire was directed toward the liberty of God—that is, into the spiritual Element—where he was <term>resigned</term> <note>original: "Resigned"; in the sense of "Gelassenheit," or total spiritual surrender to the divine will</note> in God. Then, God's loving will ruled him through the quality of the free Lubet. But he departed from the free Lubet of God and from that state of surrender, moving into a self-centered will which he forged in the center of nature. From this, pain and torture arise—namely heat and cold, as well as harshness, sour bitterness, and all the qualities of the dark compression.

But if it regains its balanced state <note>original: "Likeness"</note> in the same quality it held at the center of its "mother"—meaning, in the *Sulphur* <note>original: "Sulphur"; in Böhme’s alchemy, the material substance or "mother" that contains the life force</note>—just as she generated it in the beginning; that is, as it first emerged into natural life in both <term>Tinctures</term> <note>original: "Tinctures"; the spiritual qualities or "dyes" that give life its specific characteristics</note> of man and woman, specifically in the child where life first began to <term>Enkindle</term> <note>original: "Enkindle"; to ignite or spark into life</note>; then it is freed from all anguish. It returns again to the balanced state of heat and cold. Although this struggle begins for many even within the womb, the actual combat is only fully raised up after life begins. At the start of life, existence enters into its highest joy, for the gates of the <term>Three Principles</term> <note>original: "Three Principles"; Böhme's system of the Dark World, Light World, and the Outer World</note> are opened in perfect harmony; however, the battle for dominance between darkness and light soon begins.

<margin>* Enraged.</margin>
46. Now we must consider what should be done for <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercury"; the active, moving spirit or life-force in alchemy</note> if it becomes <margin>† with their bestial, lustful excess or disorder.</margin> * <term>Enkindled</term> (enraged) in either heat or cold, which causes sickness and pain. It would be very good if humanity possessed the right cure, but alas! It remains hidden and obscured because of the curse upon the earth and the abominations and sins of men; they awaken this poison in <term>Mercury</term> through their unrestrained † animalistic nature.

47. Yet the poor captive <note>referring to the suffering human soul or body</note> still needs deliverance. Even though we do not possess the "High Universal" <note>the Panacea or Philosopher's Stone</note>—which reaches the very center and returns the <term>Wheel of Life</term> to its original state—we must still use the fruits of the Earth’s Mercurial <term>Walm</term> <note>original: "Walm"; a surging or bubbling energy of the earth</note> for healing, since the body has also become earthly. A person must match <note>original: "accord (or Assimulate)"</note> like with like: one salt with another, depending on the type of inflammation in the body's salt. For whichever quality the <term>Brimstone</term> <note>original: "Brimstone" or Sulphur; the material substance</note> has been ignited in—whether heat or cold, melancholy or epilepsy <note>original: "falling sickness"</note>, whether the <term>Brimstone</term> is burnt out and putrefied in the body, or still burning in a cold or hot fire—the cure requires a matching herb and a matching <term>Brimstone</term>. This is necessary so that the heat or cold in the <term>Salniter</term> <note>original: "Salniter"; saltpeter, seen as a vital, explosive salt</note> (where the salt originates) is not shocked <note>original: "terrified"</note> by a foreign power entering it. Otherwise, it would generate a <term>Mort Salt</term> <note>original: "Mort Salt"; a "dead" or corrosive salt</note> and open the "House of Sadness" <note>disease or misery</note> even wider. However, an herb in its wild nature, as it grows from the surging energy <note>original: "Walm"</note> of the earth, is not powerful enough on its own. It cannot master the root of the <term>Enkindled</term> <term>Mercury</term> within the <term>Brimstone</term>; instead, it may only ignite it more violently in that same state.

48. Whatever you desire to happen to the body, that same thing must first happen to the remedy which is meant to cure the body. To cure a "foul" <note>meaning a corrupt or toxic disease</note> sickness, there must be a "foul" **Sulphur** <note>original: "Brimstone"; in Böhme’s alchemy, this represents the combustible, active substance of a thing</note>; likewise, for a cold or hot sickness, a similar nature must be understood. For in whatever degree of fire or cold **Mercury** is ignited, and in whichever form among the <term>Seven Properties of Nature</term> <note>Böhme’s system of the seven qualities that constitute all existence, from harshness to sound/light</note>—that is, whichever **Salt** among the seven salts is ignited—that specific salt is required for the cure. For sickness is nothing more than a "hunger." This hunger desires nothing but its own likeness. Now, the property of that life, which stood in "Joy" at its very beginning, is the root; sickness is its immoderate ignition <note>original: "Enkindling"</note>, by which its balance <note>original: "Temperature"</note> is broken and divided. Thus, the root in its hunger desires its likeness, but the inflammation has taken it away. Since the inflammation is stronger than the root, the hunger of the inflammation must be satisfied, and that which it is itself must be administered to it.

49. Just as God cured us with His love and restored us to the salvation of the soul after we had ignited that soul in the poisonous **Mercury** of His anger, so too must this "likeness" <note>the medicinal substance</note> be first cured and circulated in the <term>Mercurial Wheel</term> <note>the alchemical process of refining and rotating a substance through different states</note>. It must be freed from extreme heat and cold—not that these are removed (for that is impossible and would be useless), but they must be brought into their highest "Joy." Only then will it create a similar property in the **Mercury** of the **Sulphur** and **Salt** within the body. In this way, the root of life revives itself and raises up its original desire, so that the hunger of the disease vanishes as the inflammation subsides.

50. Now, it is necessary for the physician to know how to handle these medicines in their likeness, so that he does not "enrage" them or force them into a different property. In their own properties, these substances are just like a person's life. He must take care that they remain in their proper degree, just as they were originally brought forth in their "Mother" <note>the natural source or base substance</note>. Nothing can rise higher than its own hidden center; if it is forced higher, it must take on a different property. In that case, it is no longer in its own degree and lacks its proper virtue. It would have an "improper" power, which might work, but it has lost its "nature-right"—the state where it exists in joy—and is unable to perform its proper work in the <term>Assimilate</term> <note>original: "Assimulate"; a substance of the same nature or kind</note> of its own nature.

51. Therefore, there is nothing better than to let everything—

Let the thing remain in its innate, genuine virtue <note>original: "Vertue"; here meaning the inherent power or medicinal property of a substance</note>; only its "wrath" <note>the state of conflict or medicinal toxicity</note> must be changed into its own "joy," so that its own virtue—according to its better part—may be advanced into its dominion. Then, in this state of likeness, it is powerful enough to treat all sicknesses without any other mixture. For the original source within the Life desires no other multiplicity, but only its own likeness, so that it may stand, live, and burn in its own power and property.

§ 2. The power of the Most High has given to all things (even to every one according to its property) a fixed perfection, for *all was very good, as Moses says* <note>referring to Genesis 1:31</note>. However, with the Curse, the <term>Turba</term> <note>a Latin term used by Böhme to describe a state of "disturbance," "turmoil," or "interruption" in the natural order</term> was introduced, so that the properties now stand in the strife of <term>Mercury</term> <note>In Böhme’s alchemy, Mercury represents the active, moving, and sometimes volatile force of life and nature</note>. Yet in each property—in every herb, or whatever grows or arises out of the welling up <note>original: "Walm"; the bubbling or boiling movement of life</note> of the <term>four elements</term>—there is a hidden stability <note>original: "fixity"</note>. For all things that are in the four elements originally sprang forth out of the "Eternal Element," in which there is no strife, neither heat nor cold. Instead, all things existed in an equal weight of all properties in a "love-play," just as it is even now in *Paradise*. This same *Paradise* blossomed in the beginning of this world before the Curse spread through the Earth. Thus, it is still hidden in all things and may be opened by understanding and Art <note>referring to alchemy or spiritual science</note>, so that the first virtue may overcome the ignited malignity.

<margin>Or, Put his mercy into us.</margin>
§ 3. Although we as human beings do not have full power to do this by our own individual might, it may yet be done by God’s permission, for He has again turned His mercy toward us and again opened *Paradise* and its understanding within Man. If God has given us the power to become His children and to rule over the world, why then can we not rule over the Curse of the Earth? Let no one hold it as impossible; there is required only a Divine understanding and knowledge for it. This knowledge shall blossom in the <term>Time of the Lily</term> <note>Böhme’s term for a predicted future age of spiritual purity and peace</note>, and not in <term>Babel</term> <note>symbolizing the confused, worldly, and fragmented institutions of the current age</note>, for whom we have not written.

## CHAPTER XIV.

### *Concerning the Wheel of Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt; concerning the Generation of Good and Evil; showing how the one is changed into the other, and how one manifests its property in the other, and yet both remain within the first Creation in the Wonder of GOD, for His own manifestation and Glory.*

<margin>* Or, what it is.</margin>
1. This is an open gate leading from the previous description. Everyone says, "Show me the way to the manifestation of the Good." Hear and observe well, dear Reason; you yourself must be the way. The understanding must be born within you; otherwise, I cannot show it to you. You must enter into it so that the understanding of the work—in its practical art, which I do not deal with here—may be opened to you. I write only in the spirit of contemplation <note>Böhme emphasizes spiritual insight over practical laboratory chemistry</note> regarding how the generation of Good and Evil occurs. I open the fountain; he whom God has appointed for the task shall draw the water. Here, I will only describe the wheel of life * as it is in itself.

2. When I speak of Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt <note>In Böhme’s alchemy, these represent the three fundamental principles of all matter and spirit: Sulphur (the soul/fire), Mercury (the life-force/motion), and Salt (the body/physicality)</note>, I speak of only one single thing, whether it be spiritual or corporeal. All created things are that one thing, but the properties in the generation of this one thing create differences [or provide various gradual distinctions]. For when I name a man, a lion, a bear, a wolf, a hare, or any other beast—and also a root, herb, tree, or whatever may be named—it is all the same single thing.

3. Everything that is corporeal is the same being: the herbs and trees, and also the animals. However, each thing differs according to its first beginning. Just as the property in the *Word "Let it be"* <note>original: "Verbum Fiat"; the divine command of creation from Genesis</note> has imprinted itself in each thing, so is that kind in its reproduction. All things exist in their seed and procreation, and there is nothing that does not have a stability <note>original: "fixity"; a state of being chemically or spiritually "fixed" or unchanging</note> within it, whether it be hidden or manifest; for all shall stand for the glory of God.

4. Whatever has arisen from the Eternal Stability, such as angels and the souls of men, remains indestructible in its fixed being. But whatever has arisen in the unfixed being—that is, within the movement of Time—that enters again into the first motion

This happened according to the property of that same impression, and according to how the impression has introduced itself into forms, whereby the possibilities [or powers] have arisen in the impression as a Nature.

22. Now these three forms <note>These are the first three properties of nature: contraction, expansion, and the resulting rotation or anguish.</note> exist in one essence like a raging spirit. The desire impresses these properties so that a substance is made according to their nature. According to the bitter, raging spirit, there is an instigation within the essence—that is, a poison—which also imprints itself into the essence; this is why earthliness is so completely loathsome and bitter. Finally, the third form—the anguish—gives a fiery property to it. Yet, at this stage, there cannot be a physical essence; it is only a spiritual essence, the Mother to all substance.

23. The fourth form in this essence is the Fire. On one hand, it takes its origin from the dark, hard impression—that is, from the hardness and from the raging sting in the anguish, which is the "cold black fire" and the pain of the great anguish. On the other hand, it takes its origin in the Will-spirit of Nature. This spirit moves out of this hard, dark coldness and back into itself—that is, into the liberty that exists without the nature of harsh motion. It ignites that liberty—the Eternal Delight <note>original: "Lubet"—Böhme’s term for the divine "inclination" or "delight" that exists before and beyond nature.</note>—with the desire of nature through its sharpness, which it conceived in the initial impression. This results in a moving and stirring luster, for the Liberty is neither dark nor light; but because of the motion, it becomes light. Its delight brings itself into the desire for light so that it may be manifest in light and luster. Yet this cannot be achieved except through darkness, so that the Light might be known and revealed, and the Eternal Mind might find and manifest itself. For a Will is only one thing and one essence, but through multiplicity its form is revealed to be infinite and a pure wonder. We speak of this with the tongue of a child <note>original: "Babes-tongue"—suggesting he is using simple human language to describe divine mysteries beyond full comprehension.</note>, as we are only a little spark out of these great, infinite wonders.

(By inclining toward the dark desire after the desire for the light), it reaches the darkness along with the Eternal Will. The darkness reaches after the Light of the liberty but cannot attain it; for the darkness encloses itself within its own desire and makes itself dark within itself.

25. Thus, understand us correctly: There is in the *Fire* a "devouring." The *Sharpness* of the *Fire* comes from the harsh *Impression* of the *Coldness* and *Bitterness* arising from *Anguish*; and the "devouring" comes from *Liberty*, which—according to its own nature—turns the *Something* back into a *Nothing*.

26. And understand us very exactly and well: *Liberty* does not wish to remain a *Nothing*. 27. *Liberty* (which is called *God*) is the *Cause* of the *Light*, and the *Impression* of the *Desire* is the *Cause* of the *Darkness* and the painful *Source*. 33. The lower part, which is marked with this symbol <image-desc>A horizontal line over a bowl-shaped semicircle opening upwards.</image-desc>, is the first Principle. This is the Eternal Nature in its Anger, namely the Kingdom of Darkness dwelling within itself. The upper part (marked with this figure <image-desc>A cross surmounting a circle with a horizontal bar through its center.</image-desc>) is the Salniter <note>original: "Salniter"—a term Böhme uses for a spiritual "saltpeter," the explosive or active power of divine nature.</note>. The upper Cross above the Circle is the Kingdom of Glory. This Kingdom proceeds forth in the sudden burst <note>original: "Flagrat"—an explosive flash or crack, like lightning, marking a spiritual transition.</note> of Joy within the will of the free divine pleasure <note>original: "Lubet"—from the Latin *libitum*, referring to the free, joyful will of God.</note>. It emerges out of the Fire, through the luster of the Light, and into the power of Liberty. This spiritual Water, which also arises in that sudden burst of joy, is the "Corporality" or "Essentiality." Within this substance, the luster from the Fire and Light creates a Tincture <note>original: "Tincture"—the spiritual essence that gives life, growth, and color to matter.</note>—which is to say, a budding, a growing, and a manifestation of colors from the Fire and Light.

34. This form of separation between living and dead substance is the fifth Form, called the Love-desire. Its origin is from Liberty, which has introduced itself into a Desire through the Fire. This happens when the divine pleasure of Liberty enters into the beautiful and fiery elevation of Joy, becoming a flame of Love. In this Love-desire, it imprints the properties of whatever it has conceived in the Will of the Eternal Mind. This Will brings itself back into itself through the intensity of the Fire—returning, that is, to the first properties that arose in the first "Impression" (the initial movement and stirring).

Joyfulness arises out of anguish; for this is Joy: that the "Will of Nature" is delivered and freed from dark anguish. Indeed, there would be no knowledge of what Joy is if there were no painful source to compare it to. In its Love-desire, it conceives the first properties of the first Impression, which then divide themselves into five forms:
*   **From the Fire-flash into Seeing:** The "Water of Love" reaches the luster of the Tincture, which is where sight originates.
*   **From the Hardness into Hearing:** Through the penetration of the "sting" within the hardness, a sound is created even in the "Nothing" (the Liberty). The Tincture catches this sound and brings it forth in the "Water of the Desire."
*   **From the Raging-Sting into Feeling:** This allows one property to feel another. If all properties were only one thing, there would be no seeing, hearing, or feeling, and no understanding.
*   **From Assimilation into Taste:** As one property arises within another, the sense of taste emerges.
*   **From the Out-going Spirit into Smell:** As the "egress" (the outflowing) of each property enters into the others, the sense of smell arises.

35. Together, these five forms within the Love-desire (the fifth Form) create the sixth form: the Sound or Voice. This is the manifestation of all the forms within the spirit's property, which the desire for fiery light encloses within the spiritual Water.

In the Fire, it emerges from the anguish in the *Sulphur* within the forcing <term>Mercurial Wheel</term> <note>The "wheel of nature" or "Mercurial wheel" refers to the restless, rotating movement of the primary forces of nature.</note> as an impetuous, aspiring motion. The Water is its body, where it creates the boiling in the <term>Salniter</term> <note>Böhme's term for a foundational cosmic chemical principle, often likened to saltpeter.</note>, and the *Earth* is its power, where it kindles its strength and Fire-Soul.

51. There is but one single Element, and it unfolds itself in the Salnitral Flagrat into four parts. With the ignition, it produces a consuming Fire out of the Darkness and its essence. In the Flagrat of the "dying" of the Cold and the Darkness, it divides itself into essences: according to its subtlety, it becomes Water, and according to its density, it becomes Earth. Then, according to the motion in the Flagrat's warming, it becomes *Air*. The Air most resembles the original Element, but not entirely in its essence; for the [one] Element is neither hot nor cold, nor is it forcing or compulsive, but moves gently.

The origin of the *Sude* is in the original Element, from which the four elements emerge during the Flagrat.

In good things (which grow within the desire for love in the "oil of sulfur" <note>original: "oyl of Brimstone"—sulfur was often associated with the soul's fire or vital energy.</note>), it is good, powerful, and pleasant. In the <term>fire-flagrat</term> <note>A sudden, energetic flash or ignition of life-force within nature.</note>, it continually desires to rise above the gates of the fire. This is the source of the will of all devils and of all pride: the urge to ascend above the humility of love-desire. The fire serves as the trial of its essence, where we see how it clashes and consumes itself in the flash like a sudden thought.

47. Its essence does not arise from the essence of eternity, nor can it inherit it; instead, it arises in the kindling of temporal fire. However, it is perceived in the Eternal Spirit because of the lifting up of joy. But according to the essence of "mortification"—that is, the salt of the fire—it survives within the fire. This property arises from the first "desire"—the essence of the first "impression" <note>The initial contraction or cosmic densification of spirit into matter.</note>—which philosophers call **Saturn**. Therefore, salt is multifaceted. All sharpness in taste is salt. A good taste arises from the oily salt, as does a smell, which is the spirit flowing outward; in this spirit, the "tincture" <note>The spiritual quality or inner "color" of a substance.</note> appears as a luster or beautiful array of colors.

48. Understand us correctly: in the <term>fire-flagrat</term>, the Salniter is the point where properties are divided and where death and life separate. One life enters into an essence and dominion through the desire for love. The other life, in the flash of death, sinks down into a state of weakness according to the property of cold; this gives matter its weight. From the subtle parts of this process comes water; from the coarse, harsh parts comes earth; and from sulfur and mercury come sand and stones. From the subtle aspects of sulfur and mercury—their "water"—flesh is created. From the anxious darkness comes smoke or rust. But from the oily property—the desire for love—comes a sweet spiritual essence. From the spirit comes a pleasant smell, and from the movement of the fire and light comes the one pure Element. Finally, from the luster in the fire-flash, viewed in the light, comes the precious tincture. This tincture colors all oily salts, which is why pleasant tastes and smells arise.

It emerges in the fire from the anguish in the *sulfur* within the driving *mercurial wheel* <note>Böhme envisions nature as a rotating wheel of forces constantly interacting.</note> as a forceful, upward-striving motion. It is a "son" of all the properties and is also their life. The fire of all the forms provides it, and also receives it back again as its own life. Then, according to the motion in the surging of the flash, it becomes air. The air most resembles the original element, but it is not entirely identical in essence; for the one [true] element is neither hot nor cold. It is also not forceful or coercive, but moves gently.

The origin of this boiling is in the one element, from which the four elements proceed during the flash.

Every impurity <note>original: "Abominate"</note> of the oily life arises from the inward *Mercury* <note>the spirit-principle of life and motion</note> within the inward *Sulphur* <note>the soul-principle or substance of fire</note>. For sin also originates here: when the poisonous *Mercury* (which is the cause of life) turns backward in the fire-flash of the original *Salniter* <term>Salniter: the energetic "salt-peter" of nature that acts as the fuel for life's fire</term> and introduces itself again into "self-hood." This is the very origin of the "poison-life."

<margin>† Entire.</margin>
73. Every life that wishes to be without spot <margin>† Entire.</margin> must die in the "will-spirit" to nature within the fire of the impurity. It must die to the first impression of wrath and give itself forth as a resigned will through the process of mortification <term>Mortification: the alchemical and spiritual process of "death" and decay that leads to purification and rebirth</term> in the light of love. Whether it is heavenly or earthly, it must undergo that process, or else it never reaches the highest perfection of its degree. For humanity could not be helped unless the Love-Center of divine desire entered again into humanity and brought the "own life" (the human self-will) through mortification into itself. This is an exact model <note>original: "Type"</note>: whatever is to be freed from the impurity—that is, from the curse—must die to the four elements within that impurity and bring forth its higher state through the mortification of the fire in the light.

74. In the same way, there is a boiling of life-force <note>original: "Salnitral Sude"</note> in the earth, from which...

<meta>This page continues Boehme's explanation of how natural properties (herbs, metals, and living things) seek to refine themselves. He describes the spiritual mechanics of growth and the danger of "self-hood," where a will turns inward and creates conflict or "Turba" within its own nature.</meta>

<page-num>177</page-num>
<header>CHAPTER 14. The Signature of All Things <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"</note></header>

<margin>* Or, then.</margin> Metals, good herbs, and trees grow in this way; every property desires to be joined with what is similar to it <note>original: "the Assimulate"</note>. If it can reach what is similar to itself in "Sulphur" and "Mercury" through love, then it raises itself higher than its current level. This is just as the Eternal Liberty, with its longing <note>original: "Lubet"</note>, introduces the Eternal Nature through death <note>original: "Mortification"</note> into Desire, and thereby brings itself forth more highly—*that is*, in power and majesty. The same process is to be considered in all things, for all things arise out of only one Being; that same Being is a mystery of all beings, and a manifestation of the bottomless void <note>original: "Abyss"</note> into a foundational ground <note>original: "Byss"</note>.

<margin>† Or, proceeding from.</margin> 75. All things are generated out of the Great Mystery <note>original: "Grand Mystery"</note> and proceed from one level <note>original: "degree"</note> into another. Now, whatever moves forward in its natural level receives no impurity <note>original: "Abominate"</note>, whether it is in plants or animals. But whatever turns inward into its own "self-hood"—that is, into its own selfish longing—receives the impurity while passing through those levels. For each form of nature, proceeding from the Mystery, receives its own property into its "hunger," and in that it is not annoyed or bothered, for that belongs to its property.

<margin>* Text, spew out.</margin> 76. But if the Will turns back into the development of other properties, it conceives a craving <note>original: "Lust"</note>, and that craving creates a hunger, and that hunger draws a foreign essence into itself. Here, then, the impurity <note>original: "Abominate"</note> and the *Turba* <note>original: "Turba"; a Latin term for turmoil or the destructive "disturber" of natural harmony</note> are born. This is because the Will has entered a foreign essence contrary to the course of nature, and that essence is not part of its own property. This foreign essence now dominates the foreign Will and overcomes it. Now the Will must either cast it out <note>original: "spue out"</note>, or else it will itself be cast out by the foreign essence. Since this cannot happen without conflict, anger and enmity arise.

77. For the properties run back to the center of their first formation <note>original: "Impression"</note> and seek the strength and power of the "Fire," which causes heat and cold to arise in the body. These properties then act as enemies to one another, stirring up the first "Mother" <note>the formative, harsh forces of nature</note> in her most wrathful malice and spite according to that harsh formation. Then the contest for conquest begins; the property that maintains and keeps its power and dominance casts the other into the property of death—that is, into destruction <note>original: "Devoration"</note>, into the house of misery.

<summary>Boehme explains that growth and spiritual elevation occur when a being seeks its likeness through "love," but conflict and "Turba" arise when the will turns inward toward selfish desire, drawing in foreign essences that cause internal sickness and strife.</summary>

<header>The Signature of All Things <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"</note>. CHAPTER 15.</header>

### CHAPTER XV.

*Concerning the Will of the Great Mystery in Good and Evil, showing where a good and an evil Will come from, and how one introduces itself into the other.*

<margin>weaving or working property.</margin>
1. Every property takes its origin from the first—namely, from the first impression or desire toward nature, which comes out of the Great Mystery <note>original: "Grand Mystery"; referring to the *Mysterium Magnum*, the chaotic potential from which God creates the universe</note>. It brings itself forth out of itself, just as the air proceeds out of the fire. Everything that moves forward in a single will is uncontrollable <note>meaning it cannot be diverted or resisted</note>, for it does not give itself over to any other property. It dwells even from its first origin only in itself and goes forth in one single will; and this is the true way of eternity, where there is no decay <note>original: "Corruptibility"</note> if a thing remains in its own specific property. For the Great Mystery is from eternity. Now, if the form of this mystery proceeds forward and manifests itself out of itself, then this form stands with its root in the mystery of eternity. But if that form brings itself forth into a different craving <note>original: "Lust"</note>, so that two properties must dwell in one, then from that comes enmity and impurity <note>original: "Abominate"</note>. For from eternity, there has been only the one element in *motion*, and the free longing <note>original: "Lubet"; Boehme’s term for the divine, non-grasping desire or "delight" of God</note> of eternity. This longing proceeded forth with its motion from the Great Mystery of eternity as a spirit, and this spirit is God’s.

2. But when the Great Mystery once moved itself and introduced the free longing into the desire for physical existence <note>original: "Essence"</note>, then conflict <note>original: "Strife"</note> began within that desire. For out of that desire—from the element which carries only one will—there arose the four elements: namely, many different desires and wills which rule in a single body. Now there is opposition and conflict, such as heat against cold, fire against water, and air against earth; each is the death and destruction of the other. Thus, the creature that exists under this rule is nothing else but a continual state of dying and conflict. It is an enmity and a contrary will within itself, and it cannot be cured unless it enters again into a single will. This also cannot be achieved unless the variety of wills is destroyed and completely dies to the desire from which the four elements arise, so that the will becomes again what it was from eternity. In this, we humans understand what we are under this rule <note>the rule of the physical, conflicting elements</note>.

<summary>Boehme explains that while the eternal "Great Mystery" is unified, the physical world is defined by conflict because the one divine will has fragmented into the four elements. He argues that peace and eternal life are only found by dying to these conflicting desires and returning to a single, unified will.</summary>

...union of the four elements <note>The physical world according to ancient and medieval science: earth, air, fire, and water</note> is nothing else but a strife and a contrary will, a self-conflict <note>original: "self-envying"</note>, a desire for the abomination <note>original: "Abominate"; referring to the corrupted or impure state</note>, and a craving for death.

<margin>* We are our own enemies.</margin>

3. For the craving that arises out of the desire must die if the will is to be freed from the abomination and the opposing will. This is the will which proceeded out of the Great Mystery of Eternity, which the Spirit of God breathed into the image of man—that is, into the Likeness. To be freed, the desire for the four elements must die, and the will must enter again into the one only Element <note>Boehme’s term for the pure, spiritual substance of heaven, as opposed to the four physical elements</note>. It must again receive the Right of Eternity and act and go forth in one element, in the same way that God created man. But man has opposed this and brought himself into the dominion of the four elements, in which he has inherited death and also the strife within the forms of life. From this arises his sickness, loathing, and enmity. For everything that lives in God's will has not arisen in the self-will; or, if it did arise there, it has died again to its own self-centered <note>original: "self-ful"</note> desire.

4. Every will that enters into its own "selfhood" <note>Boehme uses "Self-hood" to describe the ego or the state of being focused on one's own independent existence apart from God</note> and seeks the basis of its own life-form, breaks itself off from the Great Mystery and enters into a "self-fullness." It wants to be its own master <note>original: "of its own self-ful Jurisdiction"</note>, and so it is contrary to the first Mystery, for that Mystery alone is All. This "child" of the will is accounted evil because it strives in disobedience against its own mother who brought it forth. But if the child again introduces its will and desire back into that from which it was originally generated and arisen, then it is wholly one with the source and cannot be disturbed by anything. For it enters into the "Nothing"—that is, into the Essence from which it first proceeded.

5. Therefore, O Man, understand what you must do! Behold yourself within yourself; see what you are, and whether or not you stand in the resignation <note>original: "Resignation"; Boehme’s term for "yielding" or "surrender" (Gelassenheit) to the divine will</note> of your Mother (from which you were generated and created in the beginning). See if you are inclined toward that same will. If not, then know that you are a rebellious, stubborn, and disobedient child. You have made yourself your own enemy because you have entered into self-desire and self-will. You have made yourself your own "self-centered possession," so that you cannot dwell in the first Mother, but only in yourself. For your will has entered into "selfhood," and everything that vexes, plagues, and disturbs you is only your own selfhood. You make yourself your own enemy and bring yourself into self-destruction or death.

6. Now, if you want to get out of death again, then you must wholly forsake your own self-desire, which has introduced itself

into a foreign nature <note>original: "Strange Essence"; referring to a nature that is alien to the soul's divine origin</note>, and become in *selfhood* and the self-centered desire as a "nothing," so that you no longer will or desire for yourself. 7. Without this, there is nothing but misery and death, a continual dying and perishing; for from this arises the Election of Grace <note>The theological concept of God's choice in salvation</note>. If the human will (which has departed out of the unity of eternity and entered into a self-centeredness—namely, into a selfish lust and desire) breaks itself off again from *selfhood* and enters into the death <note>original: mortification</note> of the *self-will*, and directs its desire only back into the First Mother <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "Mother" is the Eternal Nature or the divine source from which all existence originates</note>, then the First Mother chooses it again to be her child. She makes it one again with the only Will of Eternity. But that [will or person] who continues in *selfhood* continues in the eternal dying—namely, in an eternal selfish enmity. This is the only thing called "Sin," because it is an enmity against God, in that the creature wishes to be under its own self-centered command and government.

8. Thus, in its *selfhood*—that is, in a realm of conflict and strife—the creature cannot will or do anything that is good. Just as it imposes, awakens, and powerfully stirs up nothing but death within itself, so it can do nothing else for its fellow members. For from this also arises falsehood <note>original: "falshood [or lyes]"</note>, because the creature denies its union with the will of God and puts its *selfhood* in that place, so that it goes out from unity into desires and selfish lusts. If it only truly knew that all beings were its "mothers" which brought it forth, and did not hold the Mother’s substance for its own but for the common good, then greed, envy, strife, and the opposing will and enmity would not arise; from these, the anger—namely, the fire of destruction—is born.

9. All sins arise from the "self"; for *selfhood* forces itself with desire into its own self-centeredness. It creates within itself greed and envy; it draws an alien nature <note>original: "strange Essence"</note> into itself through its own desire and makes the possessor of that alien nature an enemy to itself. In this way, sin is worked with sin, and vileness with vileness; all things run confusedly in and among one another as a total abomination before the Eternal Mother.

10. In the same way, we must consider the reborn <note>original: "regenerate"</note> will, which goes out of its selfishness or *selfhood* back into surrender. That will also becomes an enemy and something loathsome to *selfhood*, just as sickness is an enemy to health, and
