# Chap. 15. The Signature of All Things <note>original: Signatura Rerum</note>

In contrast, health is an enemy to sickness. Thus, the surrendered <note>original: Resigned</note> will and the self-centered will <note>original: Self-Will</note> exist in a state of continual enmity, an incessant and lasting war and combat.

11. Self-will seeks only what serves its own self-interest <note>original: self-hood</note>. The surrendered will is not anxious at all but brings its desire solely into its Eternal Mother <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "Mother" is the divine source or Eternal Nature from which all things originate</note> so that it might be one with her. It desires to be a "nothing," so that the Mother may be everything within it. Self-will says to the surrendered will, "You are foolish to give yourself over to death, when you might instead live gloriously in me." But the surrendered will replies, "You are my abomination, my pain, and my enemy. You pull me out of eternity and into time—into nothing but perplexity and misery. You plague me for a while, and then you give my body to the earth and my soul to hell."

12. True, real surrender <note>original: Resignation</note> is the putting to death <note>original: mortification</note> of that which is an abomination <note>original: Abominate</note> against God. He who completely forsakes his self-centeredness and gives himself over—mind and desire, senses and will—to God's mercy and into the death of Jesus Christ, is dead to the earthly world in his will. He becomes a two-fold man: while the abomination within him works only toward death, his surrendered will lives in Christ’s death and continually arises in Christ’s resurrection in God. And although the self-centered desire sins—for indeed it can do nothing else but sin—the surrendered will does not live in sin. It is dead to the desire for sin and lives through Christ in God in the "Land of the Living." But self-centeredness lives in the "Land of Death"—that is, <note>original: viz.</note> in a state of continual dying and perpetual enmity against God.

13. The earthly man exists under the curse of God and is an abomination before God’s holiness. He can do nothing else but seek his own self-interest because he exists in the wrath of God. Even if he does something good, he does not do it by his own self-centered will; instead, the will surrendered to God compels him, so that he must do what his selfish nature would not willingly do. Thus, if he does good, he does it as an instrument of the surrendered will—not from his own desire, but from God's will, which guides the surrendered will in its desire as an instrument.

14. Therefore, whoever wishes to see the Kingdom of God and reach it must bring forth <note>original: Educe</note> his soul out of self-centeredness and out of earthly desire, just as a physician brings forth the cure for a disease from a painful, tormenting state and introduces it into a state of healing love <note>original: Love-desire</note>. Then, the cure also drives the sickness out of the body from its painful state and places it into a state of love. Sickness becomes the servant of medicine <note>original: Physicks</note>. Likewise, when the soul's will is cured, the evil earthly will becomes the servant of the surrendered will.

# Signatura Rerum. CHAP. 15.

15. The elemental and sidereal <note>original: Sydereal; referring to the astral or star-influenced part of human nature, which Böhme believed governed the intellect and physical instincts</note> man must only be the instrument with which man’s soul works in the resigned <note>meaning: surrendered or yielded to God's will</note> will; for God has also created it for that purpose. But the soul, following the example of Adam, has set itself up as lord and master; it has entered into its own prison and given its will over to it. If it wishes to be recognized as God’s child, it must die to that state again and be completely put to death <note>original: mortified</note> to the earthly self-interest <note>original: Self-hood</note> and desire within God’s will through Christ’s death. It must be completely born again in God’s will, stripping the earthly will of its power over self-interest, ruling over it, and guiding it in subjection and command, just as a master guides his instrument. Then self-interest loses its power and dominance, though the craving for self-interest still arises as a continual longing. This self-interest then continually longs for its own ways of life—namely, for self-glory, for earthly abundance, for envy and anger (so that it might be able to attain that abundance), and for the clever lies of falsehood. These are the life-forms of the earthly self-interest.

<margin>Voice, or breath.</margin>
16. But the resigned will, like a powerful champion, continually bruises the head of this serpent <note>A reference to the promise in Genesis 3:15 that the offspring of the woman would bruise the head of the serpent, symbolizing the soul's victory over sin</note> and says:
> *You have arisen from the Devil and God’s anger; I want nothing to do with you; you are an abomination before God.*
And even though the resigned will is sometimes captured by false desires—when those desires overwhelm and overpower it through the Devil's cravings and the suggestions <note>original: insinuation</note> of his imagination—the resigned will immediately cries out to the Word of God, so that God’s will might bring it out of the abomination of death again.

17. The resigned will has no rest here in this cottage <note>A common early modern metaphor for the physical body</note> but must always be in combat, for it is lodged in a false house. In its essence, it is in God’s hand; but outside of itself, it is in the jaws and throat of the abyss of God’s anger in the kingdom of devils, who continually pass back and forth with it, desiring to test and tempt the soul—that is, the center.

18. In the same way, the good angels also stand by the person who lives in the resigned will—that is, in the divine desire—and defend him from the poisonous imagination of the Devil. They keep off the fiery darts of the wicked one, as Saint Peter says.

19. For everything in man works and desires either God’s love or His anger. While he is in this tabernacle <note>meaning: the physical body or temporary dwelling</note>, he stands at the gate, ready to go either out or in. Both eternal principles are active within him. Whichever one the soul’s will gives itself to, by that one it is received, and to that one it is chosen. He is pulled by both, and if the soul's will remains in self-interest, then he is in the bond of God’s anger.

# Signatura Rerum. CHAP. 15.

20. But if he departs from his self-interest <note>original: Self-hood; the state of being focused on one's own ego or independent will</note> and forsakes his own desire for dominance, and continually casts himself only into God's mercy—namely, into the suffering and death of Christ, and into his resurrection and restoration—and desires nothing for himself except what God wills in him and through him, then that will is dead to the life and desire of God's anger. For it has no life of its own, but lies in the death of self-interest; and the desire of the devil and the anger of God cannot reach him. For he becomes as nothing, and yet is in God, and lives wholly in the Divine Being <note>original: Essence</note>, but not for himself. Instead, he returns to his first "Mother of Eternity" <note>the eternal source or wisdom from which all things originated</note>; he is back in the origin or place where he was before he was a created being. He exists in the will in which God created him and becomes an instrument for the voice of God, upon which only the Spirit-will of God plays, to God's own honor and for his wondrous deeds.

21. All self-centered seeking and searching within one's own ego <note>original: Self-hood</note> is a useless thing. The self-will understands nothing of God, for it is not in God, but exists outside of God within its own self-interest. But the surrendered <note>original: Resigned</note> will understands God; for the person does not do the understanding themselves, but rather it is the Spirit in whom they stand still, whose instrument they are. That Spirit reveals himself in the Divine Voice within the soul as much as he pleases. And although one might understand much through the ego by searching and learning (which is not entirely without purpose), such understanding is only external, found in the "Expressed Word"—that is, in the literal form of the text. Such a person understands nothing of the true nature of the Expressed Word or how it is grounded; for their knowledge is only born from the outward form and not from the power of the "Universal Mother" <note>original: Universal Pregnatress; Böhme’s term for the creative, life-giving power of God/Nature</note>, whose foundation has no beginning, limits, or end.

22. Now, he who is born from within, out of the speaking voice of God in God's Spirit-will, travels everywhere freely in the "Byss and Abyss" <note>original: Byss and Abyss; terms Böhme used to describe the "ground" (foundation) and the "bottomless depth" of the divine reality</note> and is bound to no outward form. For he does not walk in self-interest, but the Eternal Will guides him as its instrument, according to God's pleasure. But he who is born only in the "letter" (the literal word) is born in the form of the Expressed Word and continues in self-interest. He is a self-centered voice, for he seeks what pleases himself and argues about the outward form, while abandoning the Spirit that created that form.

23. This is exactly what "Doctor Babel" <note>A personification of the confusion and pride Böhme saw in the religious academic establishment of his day, referencing the Tower of Babel</note> is. It argues, roams, and rages about the form of the Word, and continually injects its own self-centered spirit and understanding into that form, crying out, "Here is the Church of Christ!" Yet it is only an ego-driven voice, understanding nothing of the Spirit of the form, which is beyond comprehension and plays upon its prepared instrument without limit or measure as it pleases. For conjecture, opinion, or one's own self-centered imagination—which arises in the expressed voice...

# Signatura Rerum. CHAP. 15.

[...or the literal outward Word] is not God’s Word; but that which arises in God’s Spirit in the completely surrendered <note>original: resigned</note> will, within Divine power and the Eternal Speaking Word. This Word takes its origin from God’s voice and forms the heart—specifically, a Divine desire—by which the soul's will is drawn into God.

<margin>* That Christ once died and suffered for us, etc.</margin>

24. He is a shepherd and teacher of Christ who enters through the door of Christ—that is, one who speaks and teaches by Christ’s Spirit. Without this, there is only the form—namely, the *history* <note>original: History; meaning the factual account of Christ’s life without the inward spiritual experience</note> that once took place, which a person thinks they only need to accept and comfort themselves with. But this will remains outside, for it wants to be a child of an assumed (applied) grace, and refuses to die completely to its self-interest <note>original: Self-hood; the state of being focused on one's own ego or independent will</note> within that grace and become a child of grace through the surrendered <note>original: Resigned</note> will.

25. Everything that teaches of Christ’s satisfaction <note>the theological doctrine that Christ’s death paid the debt for human sin</note> and comforting oneself with Christ’s suffering—if it does not also teach the true foundation of how a person must die completely to self-interest in that death, and give themselves up entirely in the surrendered will into the obedience of God as a new child with a new will—all of this is outside and not in the Speaking Voice of God; that is, it is not in Christ’s door.

26. No flattering or comforting is of any use. One must die to the false will and desire in Christ’s death and arise in the completely surrendered will in Christ’s resurrection within him. He must continually put to death <note>original: mortifie</note> the earthly self-interest and quench the evil that the earthly will introduces into the imagination, like an evil fire that constantly wants to burn.

27. Comforting oneself and putting the suffering of Christ in the forefront is not true faith; no, no, it is only on the outside and not within. Rather, true faith is a converted will that enters into sorrow for its earthly wickedness and wants nothing more to do with it. Yet, it finds that it is held back by the self-serving earthly lusts; therefore, with its converted will, it sincerely departs from this abomination and false desire into God’s mercy. It casts itself with great, earnest <note>original: anxious</note> desire into Christ’s obedience, suffering, and death. In the converted will, it dies completely to earthly lust in Christ’s death—never departing from it—and cries out continually: *Abba <note>original: Abba; an Aramaic word for "Father"</note>, Loving Father! Let me die in him, so that I may be nothing in myself, but live and be in his will, within his humanity in you. ## CHAPTER XVI.

->*Concerning the Eternal Signature and Heavenly Joy, and why all things were brought into Evil and Good.*<-

The creation of the whole universe is nothing else but a manifestation of the all-essential, unsearchable God. Whatever He is in His eternal, unoriginating <note>original: "un-inchoative" – having no beginning or starting point</note> generation and dominion, the creation is also of that same nature. However, the creation does not possess His omnipotence and power. It is like an apple growing on a tree: the apple is not the tree itself, but it grows from the power of the tree. In this same way, all things have sprung forth out of the divine desire and were created into a physical being <note>original: "Essence"</note>. In the beginning, no such being was present; there was only the mystery of the eternal generation, in which there has always been an eternal perfection.

2. God did not bring forth the creation so that He should become perfect through it, but for His own manifestation—namely, for great joy and glory. This joy did not first begin with the creation; no, it was from eternity in the "Great Mystery," yet only as a spiritual melody and playful activity <note>original: "Sport"</note> within itself.

3. The creation is that same playful activity outside of Himself—namely, a framework <note>original: "Platform"</note> or instrument of the Eternal Spirit, with which He creates melody. It is just like a great harmony of many different instruments, which are all tuned into one harmony. For the Eternal Word, or divine sound, or voice—which is a Spirit—has introduced itself through the generation of the Great Mystery into various forms; namely, into an "Expressed Word" or sound. Just as the joyful melody exists within the Spirit of the eternal generation, so too does the instrument—namely, the expressed form itself—which the living eternal voice guides. He plays upon it <note>original: "striketh"</note> with His own eternal will-spirit so that it sounds and makes melody. It is like an organ of many different sounds or notes that is moved by one single breath <note>original: "Ayr"</note>, so that...

<summary>Boehme explains that the creation is a manifestation of God’s internal, eternal joy and mystery, functioning like a musical instrument played by the Divine Word.</summary>

# Signatura Rerum. CHAPTER 16.

...each note, indeed every pipe, has its own unique tune, and yet there is only one kind of air or breath in all notes. This breath sounds in each note or pipe according to how the instrument or organ is constructed.

4. Thus, in eternity, there is only one Spirit in the entire work of divine manifestation. This Spirit is the Manifestor in both the Expressed Voice and the Speaking Voice of God, which is the life of the Great Mystery <note>original: "Grand Mystery"</note> and of all that is generated from it. He is the Manifestor of all the works of God.

5. All the angelic kingdoms are like a prepared work—namely, a manifestation of the eternal sound of God’s voice. They exist as specific parts of the Great Mystery, yet they are all one within the divine, eternal, speaking Word, Sound, or Voice of God; for only one Spirit rules them. Each angelic prince is a property arising from the voice of God and bears the great name of God. We see a type and figure of this in the stars of the heavens and in the kingdoms and dominions on Earth among all generations, where every lord bears his high title, respective name, and office. The stars in the firmament do the same; they are altogether one single dominion, yet they have their princely rule in the power under them. The great fixed stars bear the name and office of the forms in the mystery of the seven properties, and the others follow them as specific "houses" or divisions. In these, everyone is a unique harmony or operation, like a kingdom, and yet all proceed in a single harmony—like a clockwork which is entirely composed within itself, where all the pieces work together as one. Yet the great fixed stars keep their unique property in their essential operation, especially the seven planets according to the seven properties of nature, acting as an under-birther <note>original: "under-Pregnatress" — a secondary creative or nurturing force that brings the eternal mystery into physical form</note> of the eternal mystery, or as an instrument of the Spirit from the eternal mystery.

<margin>Good and evil</margin>
6. This birth of the *Astrum* <note>Latin: "star" or "constellation"; here referring to the celestial or astrological influence on the soul and body</note> brings forth joy and sorrow within the four elements—that is, in its body or essence. Everything is very good in itself; it is only the change in the creature that comes from a lustful imagination. Through this, the creature rouses the wrath of the fire within its properties and brings them out of the harmony of their agreement <note>original: "likeness of their Accord"</note>. Nothing is evil as long as it remains in this equal harmony. For even the worst thing, which causes sorrow when it leaves the harmony, creates joy when it remains in that state of likeness. Therefore, no creature can blame its Creator as if He made it evil; all was very exceed-

<margin>
God's presence in Satan; Devils praise God in wrath, while men and angels praise Him in love.
</margin>
7. King Lucifer stood in the highest joy at the beginning of his creation. However, he departed from that likeness to God and placed himself outside of the divine accord <note>original: "Accord [or Heavenly Comfort]"</note> and into the cold, dark, fiery generation from which hot fire arises. He abandoned his proper order and left the harmony in which God created him. He wanted to be lord over all, so he entered the dominion of the harsh fire. Now, he is an instrument within the power of that harsh fire. The all-essential Spirit strikes and sounds upon his instrument, but it sounds only according to the property of the wrathful fire. Just as the harmony—the life-form—is within each thing, so is the sound or tone of the eternal voice within it. In the holy, the voice is holy; in the perverse, it is perverse. All things must praise the Creator of all beings: the devils praise Him in the power of wrath, while angels and men praise Him in the power of love.

<margin>
The Three Principles
</margin>
8. The Being of all beings is only one single Being, but in its generation <note>meaning its manifestation or "bringing forth" into existence</note> it divides itself into two principles: light and darkness, joy and sorrow, evil and good, love and anger, fire and light. Out of these two eternal beginnings (or principles) comes the third beginning—the creation—made for God’s own play of love and melody, according to the properties of both eternal desires.

9. Thus, everything moves in its own harmony and is guided (or driven) by a single Spirit, which exists in each thing according to that thing's specific property. This is the clockwork <note>original: "Clock [or Watch-work]"</note> of the Great Mystery of Eternity in each principle, according to the property of that principle and the innate form of the instrument of those same creatures across all these beginnings.

10. Death is the boundary for all that is temporal, through which evil may be destroyed. However, whatever arises out of the eternal beginnings and enters another figure within its harmony and life-form, yet departs from God’s harmony and the true order in which God created it, is cast out of that harmony. It is cast into its own likeness, like a dissonant, clashing melody or sound within the great, excellent, well-tuned harmony. Because it is an opposite, contrary thing that carries a different tone, sound, and will, it is moved into its own likeness. Therefore, hell is given to the devil as his house and home, because he brought his life-form into the anger of God.

Essence, another falls down, and there is an incessant, lasting enjoyment and labor.

It exists as a spoken-forth breath <note>original: "out-spoken breath"</note> from the Being of all beings; not that it was made of the eternal essence itself, but out of the breathing forth [or expression] of the eternal essence—out of love and anger, out of evil and good—as a unique generation of a unique principle in the hand of the Eternal Spirit.

<margin>Anguish in hell is joy in heaven</margin>
17. Therefore, everything that is in this world is a type and figure of the angelic world. No, they are separated into two principles: in heaven everything is good, while that same thing is evil in hell. Whatever is anguish and torment in hell is good and a joy in heaven; for there everything exists in the source of light, but in hell everything exists in the wrath of the dark source.

18. Hell—namely <note>original: "viz." (videlicet)</note>, the dark world—also has its generation of fruits, and there is the same kind of essence and dominion in them as in heaven, but according to the nature and manner of the wrathful property. For the fiery property makes all things evil in the darkness, but in the light it makes all things good; in short, everything is entirely one in both eternal worlds, but light and darkness separate them. Thus they stand as an eternal enmity opposite one another, so that it may be known what is evil or good, joy or sorrow, love or anger: there is only a distinction between the love-desire of the light and the anger-desire of the darkness.

# Signatura Rerum <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"; Latin for "The Signature of All Things"</note>. CHAPTER 16.

<margin>Love-fire is poison to the devils</margin>
19. In the origin of **Eternal Nature**, in the **Father's** property in the great **Mystery** of all **beings**, it is entirely **one**. For the same single **fire** is even in the **Angelic World**, but in another **quality** <note>original: "Source"; Boehme uses this to refer to the inner quality or "source-property" of a thing</note>—namely, a **love-fire**. This is a poison and a **fire** of **anger** to the **devils** and to **hell**. For the **love-fire** is a **death**, a mortification <note>In this context, the "putting to death" or neutralizing of a lower nature</note>, and an **enmity** toward the **anger-fire**. It deprives the **wrath** of its **might**, and the **wrath** does not desire this, nor can it be otherwise. For if there were no **wrath**, there would be no **fire**, and also no **light**. If the **eternal wrath** did not exist, **eternal joy** also would not exist; in the **light**, the **wrath** is changed into **joy**. The substance of the wrathful **fire** is put to death as far as the **darkness** in the wrathful **fire** is concerned, and out of that same **dying**, the **light** and **love-fire** arise—just as the **light** burns forth from a **candle**, yet in the **candle**, the **fire** and **light** are but **one thing**.

<margin>Heaven is eternal captivity to hellish things</margin>
20. Thus also the **Great Mystery** of all **beings** is in **eternity**, in itself, only **one thing**. But in its **unfolding** and **manifestation**, it goes from **eternity** into **eternity** in two **essences**—namely, into **evil** and **good**. What is evil to one thing is good to another. **Hell** is evil to the **angels**, for they were not created for it; but it is good to the other **hellish** creatures. So also **heaven** is evil to the **hellish** creatures, for it is their poison and death, an **eternal dying**, and an **eternal captivity**.

21. Therefore there is an **eternal** enmity, and **God** is only called a **God** according to the light of His **love**. **He** is indeed Himself **all**, but according to the **darkness** He says, *"I am an angry, jealous God, and a consuming fire."* <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 4:24</note>

22. **Every creature** must remain in the place where it was conceived in its **creation** and formed into an **image**, and must not depart out of that same **harmony**, or else it becomes an **enemy** of the **Being** of all **beings**.

<margin>Yet the Devil is not happy in Hell.</margin>
23. And thus **hell** is even an **enemy** of the **devil**, for he is a strange **guest** within it—namely, a perjured **fiend** cast out of **heaven**. **He** wants to be **lord** in that for which he was not created. The whole **creation** accuses him of being a false, perjured, **apostate spirit** who has departed from his **order**. Yes, even the **nature** in the **wrath** is his **enemy**; although he shares the same property, he is still a **stranger** and wants to be **lord**. Though he has lost his **kingdom**, he is only a resident in the **wrath of God**. He who was too rich has now become too poor; he had everything when he stood in **humility**, and

# Chapter 16. Signatura Rerum <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"; Latin for "The Signature of All Things"</note>.

Now he has nothing and is, moreover, imprisoned in the abyss <note>original: "Gulf"; referring to the chaotic void or hell</note>. This is his shame: that he is a king and yet has foolishly lost his kingdom through pride. The royal nature remains, but the dominion is taken away. From a king, he has become an executioner. Whatever God’s anger seizes, there he is a judge—namely, an officer of God’s anger. Yet he must do what his Lord and Master wills.

<margin>* Balanced.</margin>
24. Human Reason most ignorantly contradicts this, saying, *"God is omnipotent and all-knowing; He has made it. He has even done with His work as He pleased; who will argue with the Most High?"* Yes, dear Reason, now you think you have hit the mark. But first, please learn the basics <note>original: "A. B. C."</note> of the Great Mystery. Everything that has arisen out of the Eternal Will—that is, out of the Great Eternal Mystery of all beings (such as angels and the souls of men)—stands in an equal balance between evil and good within the free will, just as God Himself does. Whichever desire works powerfully and dominantly in the creature, completely surpassing the other, the creature becomes that property. (As a candle puts forth a fire from itself, and out of the fire comes the wind <note>Boehme often uses "wind" to describe the "spirit" or moving air that interacts with the flame</note>, which the fire draws back into itself and yet gives forth again; when this spirit has gone forth from the fire and light, it is then free from the fire and light. Whatever property it receives again, it belongs to that property. The first mystery in which the creature exists is the all-essential mystery, and the other, in the outgoing spirit, is its own possession and a self-centered will.) Does not every angel have its own unique spirit, which is generated out of its own mystery, having its origin in eternity? Why would this spirit want to be a tempter of God and test the Mystery, which immediately imprisons it in wrath, as happened to Lucifer? It contains within itself the pull toward both God’s wrath and God’s love. Why does the spirit (which is generated out of both and is the likeness of the Spirit of God) not stay in its place in obedience, like a child before its mother in humility?

<margin>* Or, This is spoken without any foundation</margin>
25. You say it cannot be so, or that it is not so. Every spirit stands in the place where it was created in equal balance and has its free will. It is a spirit along with the all-essential Eternal Spirit and may take for itself a desire <term>original: "Lubet"; a technical term in Boehme's work meaning an inner inclination, delight, or the first movement of a will toward a certain "taste" or quality</term> within the all-essential Eternal Spirit as it chooses, either in God’s love or anger. Whichever way it directs its longing imagination, it receives the essence and property of that thing within the Great Mystery of all beings.

# Signatura Rerum. Chapter 16. <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"; Latin for "The Signature of All Things"</note>

26. In God, the "birth" <note>Boehme uses "birth" to describe the ongoing process by which God's nature is revealed</note> is manifest in both Love and Anger. Why should this not also be true in the creature, who is created out of God's essence and will—out of His voice and breath—as an image? Whatever property (or note) of that voice the creature awakens within itself, that same property sounds within and rules the creature. God’s will for the creature was only one thing: a general manifestation of the Spirit, as each creature was perceived within the property of the Eternal Mystery. Yet *Lucifer* was perceived in the good, angelic property, which clearly proves that he was an angel in *Heaven*. But his own embodied will-spirit forced itself into the wrathful Mother <note>original: "wrathful Mother"; the harsh, contractive, and dark quality of nature</note> to awaken that wrath within himself, intending to be a lord over every created being. Now, the will-spirit is free; it is the eternal source, and it may do what it wills.

27. Therefore, we must understand that it is exactly like this: the will-spirit, which originates from both Love and Anger—from both eternal principles—has surrendered itself to the Wrath. Because of this, the Wrath has powerfully gained the upper hand and dominion, shifting itself out of the equal harmony into a dissonance or discord. Thus, the spirit must be driven toward what it resembles. This is his fall, and it is also the fall of all evil people.

28. Now self-centered Reason cites the Scripture where it is written, *Many are called, but few are chosen*; also, *I have loved Jacob and hated Esau*; also, *Does not a potter have power to make from one lump of earth whatever he pleases?* I say the same thing: *that many are called, but few are chosen*. This is because they do not want to be; they surrender their free will to God’s anger, where they are seized, and so they are chosen to be *children of wrath*. Yet they were all called in *Adam* to Paradise, and in Christ to the regeneration <note>the process of being "born again" or spiritually renewed</note>. But they would not; the free will would not. It exalted itself into the wrath of God, which seized it, and so they were not chosen as children. For God’s love chooses only what is like itself, and so does God’s anger. Yet the gate of regeneration stands open even to the wicked whom the anger of God has seized. A human being has death within them, by which they may die to evil; but the Devil does not, for he was created in the highest perfection <note>Boehme suggests that because angels are pure spirits, their choice is final, whereas humans exist in a state of "death" or transition that allows for change</note>.

29. It is the same with *Jacob* and *Esau*. In *Jacob*, the lineage of *Christ* gained the upper hand in the wrestling wheel <note>Boehme’s term for the dynamic, revolving forces of nature and spirit</note>, while in *Esau*, the fall of *Adam* prevailed. Now, Christ was promised to enter humanity for this reason: so that He might heal the fall of *Adam* and redeem *Esau* (who was held captive in the wrath) from that wrath. *Jacob* signifies *Christ*, and *Esau* signifies *Adam*. Now Christ is to redeem *Adam*

# CHAPTER 16. The Signature of All Things <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"; Latin for the "signature" or outward expression of the inner essence of things</note>

<margin>* Or, die.</margin>
Adam was held captive by Death and Wrath. But did Esau continue in sin? That I do not know, and the Scripture also does not declare it. The blessing belonged to Esau (representing Adam), but he foolishly gave it away in the Fall. So, the blessing fell upon Jacob (representing Christ), who was meant to bless both Adam and Esau. In this way, the Kingdom and the Blessing could be given again as free Grace to Adam and Esau. Although he was caught in the Curse, the door of Grace stood open in Jacob—that is, in Christ. Therefore, Jacob (Christ) said afterward, once he had entered into Adam's soul and flesh:

> *Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened by your sins, and I will give you rest.* <note>original: "Come unto me all ye that are weary and heavy laden with your Sins, and I will refresh you"; Matthew 11:28</note>

Also, "I have come to call the sinner to repentance"—not Jacob, who does not need it, but Esau, who does. And when he (namely Esau) comes, then Christ says:

> *There is more joy in heaven for him than for ninety-nine righteous ones who need no repentance.* <note>original: "There is more Joy in Heaven for him, then for ninety nine Righteous ones, which need no Repentance"; Luke 15:7</note>

That is, for one Esau who repents, there is more joy than for ninety-nine Jacobs, who are already held within the lineage of Christ from the very beginning of their lives. There is more joy for one poor sinner whom Wrath has seized at the very source of life, and who seemed chosen for condemnation, if he brings his deadly sins back into the death of sin <note>Boehme refers here to the "mortification" of sin, or the process of dying to one's selfish nature</note>, than for ninety-nine righteous ones who need no repentance.

30. But who are the righteous? For we have all become sinners in Adam. **Answer:** <note>original: "Resp.", short for the Latin "Respondeo"</note> They are those whom the lineage of Christ in humanity takes hold of at the first opening of life within them. They cannot fall as Adam did, because they are held by Christ's "Will-spirit" in the "wrestling wheel"—where Love and Wrath are balanced—and are chosen for Life. This happened to Jacob, as well as to Isaac and Abel. However, this lineage was intended to be the preacher and teacher for Cain, Ishmael, and Esau, urging them to repent and turn away from the Wrath. This lineage gave itself into the Wrath that was ignited in Adam, Cain, Ishmael, and Esau, and destroyed the Devil’s sting with Love. This ensured that Cain, Ishmael, and Esau had an open gate to Grace. If they would only turn and "die in Jacob"—that is, if they would enter into Christ’s death and die to sin alongside Abel, Isaac, Jacob, and Christ—then they would be received into the "election of grace."

32. The Anger must be drowned and appeased in our human nature <note>original: "Humanity"</note>. A mere ritual offering did not do it; rather, it required a complete resignation into the Wrath so that Love might drown the Wrath. **Jacob** in **Christ** must drown **Esau** in the power of Love within his blood, so that **Esau** might also become a **Jacob** in **Christ**. But **Esau** was not willing to receive his brother **Jacob** and fought over the **birthright**. This means that **Adam** in his state of sin will not and cannot receive (or accept) **Christ**; he shall and must die to the sinful flesh and will.

33. Therefore, **Esau** has always fought against **Jacob**, because **Jacob** was meant to drown him in **Christ** through his blood. The evil **Adam** within **Esau** would not have this, for he wanted to live in his own **selfhood** <note>The state of being centered on one's own ego and desires, separated from God</note>. Therefore, he fought with the earthly **Adam** against **Jacob**. 

But when **Jacob** met him with his gifts—that is, when **Christ** came with his free gift of love into our human nature—then **Esau** fell upon his brother **Jacob’s** neck and wept. For when **Christ** entered into our humanity, **Adam** wept in **Esau** and repented of his sins and his evil intent to kill **Jacob**. When God’s Love in our humanity entered into God’s Anger, the angry Father bewailed our sins and misery. **Jacob**, through his humility, drew mournful tears out of his brother **Esau**. That is, the Love in our humanity brought forth great compassion out of and through the angry Father. 

Thus, even in the midst of his burning <note>original: "enkindled"</note> wrath within humanity, the angry Father set open a gate of mercy for **Adam** and all his children. His Love broke the Anger by entering into Death, creating an open gate to his grace for poor sinners within that death.

34. Now the poor sinner, whom Anger has chosen for the condemnation of eternal death, is commanded to enter into this same death. He must die to sin in **Christ’s** death, and then **Christ** drowns that sin in his blood and chooses him again to be God's child.

35. Here is the calling: **Christ** calls us into his death, into his dying, but the sinner wants no part of this. Now a struggle arises within the sinner between the "Seed of the Woman" and the "Seed of the Serpent." Whichever side overcomes is the one that conceives the "child" within. Now the free will may reach toward whichever it pleases; both gates stand open to him. Many who are in **Christ’s** lineage are also led into iniquity through imagination and lust, just as **Adam** was. ## CHAPTER 16. The Signature of All Things <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"; Latin for the "signature" or outward expression of the inner essence of things</note>

**Election** <note>The theological concept of being chosen by God for salvation</note> is established for him who turns away from sin; he is **Elected** who dies to sin through **Christ's** death and rises in **Christ's** resurrection. He is one who receives God in **Christ**, not only with his words <note>original: "Mouth"</note>, but in divine desire within his **Will** and **New Birth**, as a new "fiery generation." Mere knowledge cannot grasp it; only an earnest desire and the breaking of the sinful will can grasp it.

36. Therefore, there is no sufficient basis for the **Election** of grace as **Reason** <note>In this context, human logic or intellectual understanding as opposed to spiritual revelation</note> presents it. **Adam** is chosen in **Christ**, but the fact that many a twig withers on the tree is not the tree's fault. For the tree does not withdraw its sap from any twig; rather, the twig gives itself out too eagerly with its own desire. It runs on in its own self-will—namely, as it is consumed by the "inflammation" or scorching of the sun and fire—before it can draw sap again from its mother and refresh itself.

37. In this same way, man perishes among evil company in wicked, vain ways. God offers him his **Grace** so that he might repent; but evil company and the **Devil** lead him into wicked ways until he is too deeply imprisoned in the **Anger** <note>A term often used by Boehme to describe the wrathful or harsh aspect of nature and divine judgment</note>. Then it becomes very difficult for him. He was indeed called, but he is evil. God chooses only children; because he is evil, the choice passes over him. But if he reforms and amends his life, the **eternal Choice** (or **Election**) receives him once again.

<margin>* Text,</margin>
38. Thus the Scripture says, *“Many are called”*; but when the choice through **Christ’s** suffering and death comes upon them, they are not capable of receiving it because of their self-centered, stubborn, evil will. Thus, they are not the **Elected**, but evil children. And here it is rightly said: *“We have piped to you, but you have not danced; we have mourned to you, and you have not lamented for us. O Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered your children together, as a **clock-hen** <note>original: "clock-hen"; an archaic term for a mother hen or brood hen</note> gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!”* It is not said, "you *could* not," but "*you would not*." And while they remain in the iniquity of sin, they also *cannot*; God will not cast his pearl before swine. But to the children who draw near to him, he gives the pearl and his bread.

39. Therefore, whoever blames God despises the mercy which he has introduced into **human nature** <note>original: "Humanity"</note>, and brings judgment headlong upon his own body and soul.

40. Thus I have truly warned the reader and set before his eyes what the **Lord of all Beings** has given me. He may behold himself in this **Looking-Glass** <note>mirror</note> both within and...

# The Brief Summaries of What the Several Chapters Discuss.

**Chap. I.** How everything spoken about God without the knowledge of the Signature is silent <note>original: "dumb"</note> and lacks understanding; and how the Signature lies very accurately composed within the mind of man, according to the Being of all Beings.

**Chap. II.** On the opposition and conflict within the Essence of all Essences, through which the foundation <note>original: "ground"</note> of sympathy and antipathy in Nature may be seen, as well as the corruption and cure of every thing.

**Chap. III.** On the Great Mystery of all Beings.

**Chap. IV.** On the birth of the four elements and stars, within the metallic <note>original: "metaline"</note> and created <note>original: "creatural"</note> properties.

# The Postscript.

*Reader,*

It would be too tedious, and even unnecessary, to give you a brief summary of the specific chapters of this book; for the work itself is a short, hidden signature or character of natural and divine knowledge. Therefore, a careful and insightful reading of the whole text will be your best index. This author is not meant to be read sporadically or in piecemeal fashion, for he does not create a controversial, academic collection <note>original: "rapsode," referring to a patchwork or medley of various sources</note> of different authors. Instead, there is one continuous breath and sound of his own experimental knowledge running as a harmonious melody through all the *Three Principles of Divine Manifestation*. With sweet accord, it plays interchangeably upon all the three clefs <note>original: "cliffs," a musical metaphor for the fundamental keys or starting points</note> of *philosophy*, *divinity*, and *theosophy*, from the deepest bass to the smallest or highest note that can be reached by the spirit of man.

Therefore, none will understand him except the children <note>original: "nurslings"</note> of *Sophia* <term>Sophia: the Greek word for "Wisdom," often personified in mystical literature as Divine Wisdom</term>, in whose souls the air of the one pure element of *Paradise* breathes. This air reconciles <note>original: "atone," used here in the sense of making "at one" or bringing into harmony</note> the strife of the four elements and revives the soul's true magical fire, by which it is able to test all things and hold fast to that which is good. In a word, it brings the soul's true faith, working through love, into the "Nothing," where it loses its own selfish "something" and finds all things.

I know this book will seem strange and simple to the proud, self-conceited sophisters <term>Sophisters: people who use clever but false arguments, especially for deceptive purposes</term>, the wiseacres of pedantic reason, who will quibble and complain about anything that does not "dance to their pipe." But I do not value their criticisms; rather, I pity their "learned-by-the-letter" mock-sciences, which are merely the shadows they chase from their own distracted imagination. Such as these, being imprisoned in the mystery of *Babel* <note>original: "Babel," symbolizing confusion, false religion, and the division of languages/understanding</note>, follow only after their beast, *Mammon* <term>Mammon: a biblical term for wealth or greed, personified as a false god</term>, upon which they ride in pride. They scorn anything that does not please and flatter them in their admired works of greedy iniquity, which they gild over with a facade of holiness. But the *Babylonian* structure of their "Great Turmoil" miracles <note>original: "Turba Magna," a term used by Boehme to describe the chaotic, wrathful disturbance in nature or the soul</note> will fall when it has reached the highest limit of its constellation, and no human wit shall be able to prop it up. In the meantime, the *Antichrist* in Babel will rage, dominate, and carry out the sentence of wrath, or his own dismal doom, upon himself.

But I will not overstep by wandering too far; instead, I will proceed to

...my intent is to explain to you some words that I have used in this translation, such as *Flagrat*, *Lubet*, *Source*, and *Sude*.

### *The Translator's Explanation of the Word "Flagrat"*

The word in German <note>original: "Germane"</note> is *Schreck* <note>original: "Schra'ck," meaning a fright, shock, or sudden terror</note>, which properly signifies a fright, sudden astonishment, or dismay. In other books, it is translated as "terror" or "crack"; but I have used the term *Flagrat*, from the Latin word *flagro* <note>meaning "to burn" or "to blaze"</note>. Although I do not mean an actual burning by it, I mean the powerful opening of either life or death during the enkindling of the fire in Nature. For this fire is the dividing boundary where the life of both "Principles" is opened and separated: the life of the first is the "dying death" in the darkness, and the life of the second is the "living life" in the Light. 

You may perceive a resemblance of this *Flagrat* in thunder and lightning, or in gunpowder and the like. For example, take various sulfurous and saltpeter <term>Salnitral: relating to saltpeter (potassium nitrate), a key ingredient in explosives</term> minerals mixed exactly together. Currently, their powers are, as I might say, contracted or shut up in the "astringent dark desire" or death. But touch them correctly with the true fire, and you will see how they will soon open, disclose, and flash forth—even displaying and streaming themselves out into various properties, colors, and virtues. It is essentially the bursting forth of the "ardent desire" in Nature. It is, as I may term it, the "magical fire-breath," by which the powers of either light or darkness are startled <note>original: "dismayed," used here to mean overwhelmed or shocked into a new state</note>. In brief, it is the pregnant echo of the sound of Eternity everywhere speaking, working, and opening itself in love or anger, in each thing according to its will and desire. In some, it is the horrible *Flagrat* leading to death, and in others, it is the pleasant, triumphant *Flagrat* leading to life.

->*Lubet*<-

The word in the "Dutch" <note>In the 17th century, "Dutch" often referred to *Deutsch* (German)</note> is *Lust*, which signifies a longing, desire, or inclination toward a thing; it also means a delight, pleasure, or contented joy. Sometimes it refers to "imagination and desire." However, because our English word "lust" is commonly used in the worst sense (namely, for a longing after evil and vanity) and would not properly agree with or fully express the German word *Lust* in all places, I have generally translated it as *Lubet*, from the Latin word *lubitum* <note>meaning "pleasure" or "will"</note>. 

By this is meant the divine *beneplacitum* <note>Latin: "good pleasure" or "favorable decree"</note>, or good pleasure. By it is understood the original source of a desire within the "eternal nothing" or "pregnant magic"—God’s free approval of the desire to manifest Nature and creatures, without which all would have remained an eternal stillness in the "nothing." This *Lubet* in man is the moving will toward...

# The Postscript

->Good or Evil, Light or Darkness, Love or Anger.<-

### Source

By this is meant the first original qualities or properties of both the inward Principles, as they break forth in the *Sude* <note>original: "Sude"; the boiling or seething process of natural forces described below</note> of the fire—whether in the *Flagrat* <note>original: "Flagrat"; the sudden flash or ignition of power</note> of Love or Anger, within Nature or a creature. In the Darkness, the Love-*Ens* <term>Ens: a philosophical term meaning "essence" or "being"</term> (or paradisiacal light) is shut up in death, which causes a harsh, dark "Source": a state of pain, horror, torment, or unrest. This is the fundamental property of the conflicting elements and stars under the curse of God. 

In the Light, however, the life of Love breaks forth and swallows up this wrathful "Source" of darkness and death, turning it into joy or a divine "Source." Therefore, by the word *Source*, you should understand the original quality, property, or condition of evil, darkness, anger, sorrow, cursing, damnation, and death—or the opposite of these in their divine "Source" or essential working property, occurring in both time and eternity.

### Sude

The word *Sude* is German <note>original: "Germane"</note> and signifies a boiling or seething. It refers to the stirring of the "Seven Properties" in Nature, arising from the assimilation or essential combined influence of the outward and inward *Sol* <note>original: "Sol"; the Sun, representing the divine light or spirit</note> within *Sulphur* <note>original: "Sulphur"; in Boehme’s alchemy, this represents the substance or "burning" quality of nature</note>. From this process, the flowering vegetation of the earth proceeds; likewise, the generation of metals and minerals lies within this "seething."

These are some unusual words which I have used in rendering this book into English. It is not that I wish to make a "strange translation" <note>original: "Strange-Lation"</note> or be a coiner of new words merely to confuse the mind, but rather to express the author’s intent and scope as well and as accurately as I could. I cannot say I have everywhere achieved a full and lively expression of the author's meaning; for as Nature opened its knowledge within him, so too did it open its language. Consequently, in some words, there may be a specific and peculiar *Idea* <note>original: "Idea"; a spiritual concept or form</note> which our English words perhaps do not fully express in certain places. 

Yet, I hope no one shall find the author's sense falsified or perverted, but truly translated according to the original copy I possess. Words are but *vehicles of things* <note>original: "Vehicula rerum"</note>; they are formed to express realities, and not just bare sounds or empty air. Now, he who rightly understands the foundation of the *Kabbalah* <note>original: "Cabala"</note> and *Magic* <note>original: "Magia"; here meaning spiritual or divine wisdom</note>, and knows how the "Language of Nature" speaks in every tongue, may well translate this author. However, the bare letter of his writings—no matter how exactly translated—will not give a person the understanding of them. That understanding comes only through the Spirit of Regeneration in Christ, in whom the fullness of the Deity dwells bodily.

I would be glad if anyone would take the pains to amend what I have done incorrectly and make these writings easier for those of a common <note>original: "vulgar," meaning ordinary or non-specialist</note>

### The Various Names and Titles of the Author’s Books, Collected from His Writings and Organized into Seven Parts.

The first book, called *The Dawn* <note>original: *Aurora*, or *The dawning of the Eternal Day*</note>, was written in the year 1612. It was taken from him before it was finished and kept by the magistrates of Görlitz <note>original: "Gerlits"; a town in Germany where Boehme lived</note>, with strict commands that he should not meddle in writing books, as it did not belong to his profession <note>original: "Vocation"; Boehme was a shoemaker by trade</note>. Because of this, he refrained from writing for seven years. But afterward, being stirred up by the prompting of the Divine Light, he proceeded to write and supplied what was lacking in the first book within his second, third, and fourth books. *The Dawn* climbs up out of its infancy and shows you the creation of all beings, yet very mysteriously and without sufficient explanation; it has a deep and symbolic meaning, and within it are contained many mysteries that are yet to come to pass.

The second book is called *The Three Principles*. It is a key and an alphabet for those who wish to understand his writings. Within it, the Great Mystery has somewhat opened itself. It treats the eternal birth and generation of the Deity; also the creation, the paradisiacal life of man, and the Fall. Likewise, it covers repentance, justification, and the regeneration of the two testaments of Christ, and the total salvation of man. It is an eye with which to look into the wonders of the divine mystery.

The third book is called *The Threefold Life*. It is a key for all mysteries, both above and below. It shows the entire foundation of the *Three Principles* and serves everyone according to their own essential nature <note>original: "property"; in Boehme’s philosophy, this refers to the specific spiritual qualities or "properties" that make up an individual's soul</note>. Within it, a person may find the depth and resolution of any question that human reason is able to devise or propose. It is an open gate to the Great Mystery, and it is truly a wonder that surpasses the capacity of reason; within it are revealed and laid out the deep mysteries and secrets about which the...

<header>The Post-script.</header>

The world has struggled since the heavy fall of Adam, and yet such a foundation <note>original: "ground"</note> has not been brought to light until now. This, however, will not be understood by the world, but only by the children of God.

The fourth book is titled *The Forty Questions*. They were sent to him by a learned man who asked him to answer them according to his spiritual gifts. The questions explore the great depths of the origin of the soul and all the secrets of the Divine Mystery. The answers provided are such that the world might rejoice, if the envy of the devil did not hinder it; but God’s purpose shall prevail. This book provides a fundamental explanation of everything that is necessary for a person to know. Each book, starting from the first, is grounded ten times more deeply than the last, so that the fourth is a clear mirror in which the Mystery is sufficiently understood. 

If it were possible to have comprehended and written everything, it would have been three times larger and more deeply grounded. However, that was not possible, and therefore more than one book was written, so that what could not be explained in one might be found in another. It would be well if all were brought into one and the rest set aside; for the variety of books causes conflict and incorrect, confused understandings. This happens because of the captivating notions and guesses of human reason, which is not yet able to discern or see into the center and depth of the Mystery. Therefore, reason often assumes that the writing is contradictory, whereas it is not contradictory at all, but fully agrees as one in the depth. 

Yet know that there is but a glimpse of the Mysteries in these writings, for no one can truly write them down. If anyone is considered worthy by God to have the Light kindled in their own soul, they shall see, taste, smell, and hear unspeakable things concerning this knowledge. For there is the Theosophical <term>theosophical: relating to divine wisdom or direct knowledge of God</term> School of Pentecost, where the soul is taught by God, and the way into this school is faithfully described here. Is it not written, *“They shall all be taught by God, and know the Lord”*? Also, *“I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh,”* etc. Why then should anyone mock and despise it when God allows a humble layman to know Him and His Mystery? He must write higher than the reach of any natural, outward reason—even deeper than the foundation of this world! 

Therefore, let everyone open their eyes wide and see the basis of academic disputes <note>original: "school-contentions"</note>, which for the most part in all ages have produced nothing but pride, greed, envy, and wrath. In doing so, they have erased the A-B-C <note>meaning the basic principles</note> of love and a divine life, which ought to have been written and read in their own "book"—the heart. Indeed, that inner book contains more than can be expressed in the letters of any printed book, and he who can read that correctly needs no other. For within it lies the anointing <note>original: "unction"</note> from the Holy One, which teaches him the truth about all things.

# The Post-script.

Whoever applies themselves correctly to understand the Center of all Beings, and once comes to see the *Three Principles of God’s manifestation*, will not need his or any man’s writings; for he will know the Lord within himself. This is the true *constant companion* <note>original: "Vade mecum," Latin for "go with me"</note>, which surpasses the treasure of the world. Indeed, it gives such an abundance <note>original: "plero-phory," from the Greek "plerophoria," meaning full assurance or overflowing fullness</note> of joy in the hidden man that it cannot be compared with anything except the blooming spring of harmonious delights in the Eternal Paradise of God. For herein lies the true, noble Philosopher's Stone <note>In alchemy, a legendary substance that turns base metals into gold; here used as a metaphor for spiritual enlightenment</note>, which gives a person the certainty of all things and frees them from all troubles and perplexities in religious controversies. It opens the highest Mystery to them, brings the work for which nature has chosen them to the highest perfection, and gives them the power to look into the heart of everything.

<margin>I.</margin> These four books—namely <note>original: "viz.," short for the Latin "videlicet"</note> the *Aurora*, the *Three Principles*, the *Three-fold Life*, and the *Forty Questions*—along with the author's *Key* <note>original: "Clavis," Latin for "key"</note>, would make up one part. If there should be another edition, it would be good if the *Aurora* were translated and the rest exactly corrected and printed together; they would consist of about 847 sheets.

<margin>II.</margin> The second part might contain these pieces: namely, the *Six Great Points*, the *Six Small Points*, the *Signature of All Things* <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"</note>, and a *Treatise on the Heavenly and Earthly Mystery*, as well as the *Table or Scheme of the Three Principles of Divine Manifestation*.

The *Six Great Points* treat the greatest depths and secrets: namely, how the *Three Principles* mutually beget and bear each other, so that in eternity there is no strife, and yet each principle exists within itself (in its own characteristic property) as if it were solitary and alone. They also show where strife and disunity arise, and from where good and evil take their origin—brought forth entirely out of the foundation <note>original: "ground"</note> (that is, out of the Nothing into the Something) and into the foundation of Nature. This book is such a mystery—though set forth in plain simplicity—that no sharp human reason shall fathom or understand it without Divine Light. It is a key to all things.

The *Six Small Points* are a short exposition on:
1. The water and blood of the soul.
2. The election of grace, and of good and evil.
3. Sin—what it is and how it becomes sin.
4. How Christ shall deliver up the Kingdom to his Father.
5. Magic <note>The author refers to "Magick" as a spiritual or metaphysical force of the will and desire, rather than stage magic</note>—what it is and what the magical foundation is.
6. The Mystery—what that is.

The *Signature of All Things* <note>original: "Signatura Rerum"</note> deciphers the creation in its characters and forms, and shows the beginning, ruin, and cure of everything. It enters entirely into the eternal, and also into

The *Treatise of the Heavenly and Earthly Mystery* is a short and deep summary, showing how the heavenly and earthly mysteries exist within each other, and how the heavenly is manifested in the earthly. It describes the great city of Babel <note>In Boehme’s writing, "Babel" represents the confused, divided state of the formal church and the "spirit of this world"</note> overspreading the face of the whole earth in its various forms and wonders, from its very rise to its downfall. The *Table of the Three Principles* is a map or scheme of the threefold world, or an explanation of the Four-Letter Name of God <note>original: "Tetragrammaton," the Hebrew name for God, YHWH</note>, the Great World <note>original: "Macrocosmos," the universe</note>, and the Little World <note>original: "Microcosmos," the individual human being</note>. These five treatises together would contain about 60 sheets <note>A "sheet" refers to a printer's unit of measurement for the length of a book</note>.

<margin>III.</margin>
The third part might consist of these books, namely: *The Incarnation of Christ*; *The Way to Christ*; *The Book of Election*; and *The Four Complexions*.

The book of the *Incarnation* consists of three parts. The first shows the mystery of Christ’s conception and birth; the second deals with the passion, suffering, and death of Christ, and shows how a person must enter into Christ’s death and both die and arise again in and with him—explaining also why Christ had to die. The third part treats the "Tree of Christian Faith."

<margin>The Book of Election</margin>
*The Way to Christ* is a general title and contains these treatises, namely: 1. *Of Repentance*. 2. *Of Regeneration*. 3. *Of Resignation*. 4. *Of the Supersensual Life*. 5. *A Dialogue Between the Illuminated and Un-illuminated Soul*. The book of the *Election of Grace* is one of the author's clearest books; it shows the depth and mystery of election and reprobation <note>The theological debate over who is chosen by God for salvation (election) or rejection (reprobation)</note>. It reconciles the seemingly contradictory passages of Scripture based on the true underlying principles. It gives a full and fundamental satisfaction to the true Christian mind and frees it from all those wild, strange Calvinist ideas <note>original: "Calvinistical conceits"</note> which indeed hold the mind captive in the mystery of Babel.

The book of the *Four Complexions* <note>The "four complexions" refers to the four temperaments (choleric, melancholic, sanguine, and phlegmatic) believed to govern human nature</note> is a short treatise. It is an "Epistle of Consolation against Temptation." It shows where sadness and melancholic dejection of the soul come from, and how it is to be resisted and remedied. These treatises would be about 80 sheets.

<margin>IV.</margin>
The fourth part might be the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>, which is a commentary upon the First Book of Moses called *Genesis*. In this work, the kingdom of nature and the kingdom of grace are set forth in their various rules and hierarchies. It runs through all the movements of time and centers in eternity; this will be about 400 sheets.

<margin>V.</margin>
The fifth part might consist of his *Apologies* <note>formal written defenses of his ideas against critics</note>, namely: one to Balthazar Tilken contained in two parts. ### The 177 Theosophical Questions of Jacob Boehme

1. What is God in himself, without nature or creatures?
2. What is the abyss <note>A term Boehme uses for the "Ungrund," the bottomless, unsearchable nothingness out of which all existence arises</note> of all things, where there is no creature—being the abyssal (or unsearchable) nothing?
3. What is God's love and anger? How is he an angry God, seeing he is unchangeable love?
4. What was there before the angels and creation existed?
5. What is the foundation and essence from which the angels were created? What was that same power in the Word which went forth and became creaturely?
<margin>VI</margin> 6. What do the angels do in their service? And why did the power of God bring itself into distinct forms?
7. What moved Lucifer so that he lusted against God and turned himself away from the good?
<margin>V</margin> 8. How could an angel become a devil? Or what is a devil? In what essence and being does he now exist after the Fall?
9. Why did God—being almighty—not withstand Lucifer and hinder him from becoming a devil?

### The 177 Questions

**83.** Why did God place a mark on *Cain*, and say, *Whoever slays Cain, his blood shall be avenged sevenfold*? <note>original: "He that slayeth Cain, His blood shall be avenged seven-fold"</note>

**84.** Why did *Lamech* (*Cain’s* descendant) say to his wives, *Zillah* and *Adah*, *Lamech shall be avenged seventy-sevenfold*? What does this mean and signify?

**85.** What was the greatest sin of the first world? <note>This refers to the world before the Great Flood.</note>

**86.** What is the *Enochian* <note>original: "Henochian"</note> life? What became of *Enoch*, and also of *Moses* and *Elijah*? <note>original: "Henoch... Elias"; these figures were traditionally believed to have been taken by God or translated to heaven without a typical death.</note>

**87.** What does *Noah’s* Flood <term>typify</term> and point out? <note>To "typify" means to serve as a symbolic representation or spiritual foreshadowing of a later event.</note>

**88.** What does *Noah’s* drunkenness signify, because of which he cursed his son *Ham*?

**89.** What is the Tower of *Babel*; and why were the languages <note>original: "Speeches"</note> altered there?

**90.** What was the Covenant with *Abraham* concerning the blessing, and also the circumcision?

**91.** What <term>figure</term> <note>meaning a symbolic prefiguration or spiritual type</note> is the destruction of *Sodom* and *Gomorrah*; how was it carried out?

**92.** Why was *Lot’s* wife turned into a pillar of salt; how is it to be understood?

**93.** Why did the daughters of *Lot* lie with their father, after first making him drunk so that they might conceive children by him, from whom arose two powerful nations? What does this <term>figure</term> signify?

**94.** What does the <term>figure</term> of *Moses* signify—that he must be drawn out of the river and be appointed <note>original: "preferred"</note> to such a great office?

**95.** Why did the Lord appear to *Moses* in a burning bush <note>original: "fire-flaming bush"</note> when He chose him?

**96.** By what power did *Moses* perform his wonders before *Pharaoh*?

**97.** What <term>figure</term> is the departure of the children of *Israel* out of *Egypt*?

**98.** Why did *Moses* have to remain forty days upon Mount *Sinai* when God gave him the Law?

**99.** What is the Law in summary? <note>original: "in one Sum"</note>

**100.** What were the offerings of *Moses*? How was sin blotted out and <term>appeased</term> <note>original: "appeased"; referring to the theological concept of propitiation or making amends through sacrifice</note> through these offerings?

**101.** What is the foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note> of the prophetic prophecies? By what knowledge and Spirit did the prophets in the Old Testament prophesy?

**102.** Who <note>original: "What"</note> is *Christ*, of whom the prophets prophesied in the Old Testament?

**103.** Who was *John the Baptist*, *Christ’s* forerunner?

**104.** What kind of Virgin was *Mary* (in whom God became Man) before she conceived?

**105.** Why did *Mary* have to be first betrothed <note>original: "espoused"</note> to *Joseph* before she conceived by the Holy Spirit? <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note>

## The Author's Preface to these Questions.

Reader,
**I**t is written: The natural man understands nothing of the Spirit of God; it is foolishness to him, and he cannot grasp <note>original: "apprehend"</note> it. It is also written: The Spirit of God searches all things, even the depths of the Godhead <note>original: "Deity"</note>.

<margin>* Sophister <note>A "sophister" refers to someone who uses clever but fallacious arguments; a person who relies on human logic rather than spiritual insight.</note></margin>
Now, if "Mr. Wiseling" <note>original: "Wiseling"; a derogatory term for someone who thinks they are wise but lacks true understanding.</note> without Divine Light should undertake to clarify and explain these Questions, he shall not be able to do it. Indeed, perhaps he may even consider it a sin to ask such deep questions, since he himself cannot understand them.

Therefore, we tell him to leave them alone. Leave them for those to whom God’s Spirit (which searches all things through the spirit of man) shall give understanding; for to the worldly-wise person, it is an impossibility, and it even seems impossible to him.

<margin>* I do not know which book the author means, unless he is speaking specifically of this *Book of the 177 Questions*, and speaks of it intentionally. But if he did finish his answer to all these questions, the rest are either lost or withheld; for we have only 14 fully answered, and the beginning of the 15th. Yet in his other writings, he has truly and fundamentally answered these questions—even more than human Reason can ask.</margin>
But to those who love Jesus, we say [and declare] that these matters may very well be searched out and understood, and that it is no impossible thing. For in a true Christian dwells Christ, in whom all the treasures of hidden wisdom are revealed <note>original: "manifest"</note>. The Christian knows them only through the Spirit of Christ, and not by his own self-centered <note>original: "self ful"</note> nature and ability. As we have also clearly explained and described these questions in a specific <note>original: "peculiar"</note> book—briefly, it is true, and yet in our other writings extensively and sufficiently enough—I commend the reader to the Revelation of Jesus Christ.

<summary>The author explains that these theological questions cannot be understood by human reason alone, but only through the Holy Spirit dwelling within a believer. He notes that while this specific book contains only a portion of the answers, his complete theology addresses them all.</summary>
<keywords>Holy Spirit, divine wisdom, Sophister, Jacob Boehme, reason vs. faith, 177 Questions, Christian mysticism</keywords>

He who reads this *Author’s* books,
Needs a *Divine Light* in his heart;
Or else his *Reason* will only *stray*,
And *grope* for *light* in the *middle of the day*.
But no one will criticize or scorn him,
Who is truly born of *Sophia* <note>original: "Soph-jah"; a combination of Sophia (Divine Wisdom) and Jah (God).</note>;
For he who understands the meaning,
Is freed from the *Antichrist's* bonds,
And truly learns how to *see*
Into the *Divine Mystery*.

Eternal One! The Nothing and the All,
Give *Adam* <note>A symbolic reference to fallen humanity.</note>, faint and sick, a *restorative medicine* <note>original: "Cordial"; a stimulating medicine or drink intended to revive the heart and spirits.</note>;
In his diseased age and final distress,
Open the treasury of your goodness.
Oh, make his clashing spirits harmonize,
And give us the harmony of your true Word.
->*Amen.*<-
